no-fixed-block-boundaries-in-sstable.text: Both SSTable implementations write variable-length records contiguously with no fixed-size block structure, making mid-file resynchronization after corruption impossible — a corrupted length field causes the reader to consume all subsequent valid records as garbage.

no-fsync-before-wal-truncation.text: Already covered by existing `btree-wal-truncate-before-data-sync` and `lsm-compaction-deletes-without-fsync-barrier` which document this missing fsync gap in both engines

no-high-key-fence.text: No node stores a high-key (upper-bound fence key); searchers cannot detect mid-split state, which would be required for Lehman & Yao's concurrent search protocol

no-high-key-per-node.text: Nodes store no upper-bound "high key," so a reader cannot detect that a concurrent split moved keys to a right sibling; this is the second missing prerequisite for Lehman-Yao's single-latch protocol

no-leader-lease-in-codebase.text: Neither the Raft nor TOB implementations include leader lease or ReadIndex optimizations; all read and write operations pay full consensus cost.

no-leak-detection-mechanism.text: The B-tree has no allocation bitmap, page-reachability check, or post-recovery consistency scan to detect leaked or orphaned pages; once a page is lost between the tree and the free list, it is silently unrecoverable.

no-leveldb-source-in-repo.text: Trivially obvious — this is a Python reference implementation repo, not a LevelDB fork; stating the absence of C++ source is not useful for working in the codebase.

no-o-direct-usage.text: No file in the ddia-implementations codebase uses `O_DIRECT`, `os.open()`, or any `os.O_` flags; all I/O goes through Python's buffered `open()` and the kernel page cache

no-operational-path-to-correctness.text: There is no operational path to system correctness: the system has no stable regime at any scale (storage degrades monotonically, failures widen the correctness gap, no paradigm is both scalable and self-healing), AND even if a stable state existed, correctness could not be verified (the gap between specification and implementation widens under every failure mode and testing validates the wrong model).

justifications.label: No stable regime to converge toward combined with unfalsifiable correctness claims creates a logical cul-de-sac — the system cannot reach correctness and cannot detect whether it has

no-page-size-enforcement-in-serialize.text: Neither _serialize_internal nor _serialize_leaf checks whether the serialized output fits within page_size; overflow prevention is the caller's responsibility via the max_keys limit in BTree._insert.

no-persistence-api-exists.text: Too broad — a grep returning zero matches for persistence keywords across the entire project is an observation about the current codebase state, not a durable invariant; also overlaps with `mvcc-no-persistence` and `es-snapshots-are-in-memory-dicts`

no-platform-specific-sync.text: The F_FULLFSYNC claim is covered by existing `apfs-masks-linux-fsync-bugs`; the fdatasync claim is captured below as `fdatasync-never-used`.

no-pytest-config-exists.text: The repository contains no `pyproject.toml`, `pytest.ini`, `setup.cfg`, or root `conftest.py`; pytest runs with pure default settings

no-refcount-in-codebase.text: No file in the repository implements reference counting on SSTable files, Version objects, or any storage-layer snapshot structure

no-rocksdb-bottommost-level-enum.text: Trivial negative claim; `sstable-compaction-manager-lacks-bottommost-detection` already captures the important absence.

no-safe-operating-mode-exists.text: The system has no safe operating mode in any scenario: it is unsafe under concurrent access (both read and write paths lack synchronization across core components) AND unsafe during crash recovery (no storage engine has a fully safe recovery path), meaning correctness is unachievable whether the system is running normally under load or recovering from failure.

justifications.label: Concurrent operation is unsafe and crash recovery is unsafe closing both operating mode escape hatches

no-schema-validation.text: The batch pipeline performs no validation that adjacent stages produce/consume compatible record formats; mismatched tuple shapes fail at runtime with indexing errors

no-shadow-paging-implementation-exists.text: The codebase contains no copy-on-write or shadow paging implementation; all three storage engines use write-ahead logging exclusively for crash recovery

no-sibling-sentinel-is-max-uint32.text: `NO_SIBLING = 0xFFFFFFFF` marks the end of the leaf sibling chain; a leaf with this value is the rightmost at its level

no-sibling-sentinel-value.text: The sentinel NO_SIBLING = 0xFFFFFFFF marks the rightmost leaf in the B-tree.

no-storage-paradigm-is-both-scalable-and.text: No storage paradigm offers both scalability and structural resilience: hash indexes are memory-bound, LSM miss-probes are linear due to missing Bloom integration, and all paradigms degrade monotonically after crashes with no safe recovery path (crash-unsafe compaction, incomplete CRC, replay without batch atomicity).

justifications.label: Scalability walls and absent self-healing leave every storage option fundamentally limited

no-structured-topology-support.text: The codebase has no ring, star, or mesh topology modes for gossip; peer selection is always uniform random from all active nodes.

no-subsystem-has-viable-recovery-strateg.text: No subsystem at any architectural tier has a viable recovery strategy: storage-layer recovery is paradoxically over-engineered in infrastructure and under-implemented in usage (WAL builds complete but unused sequence/checkpoint machinery, with no safe crash recovery path), while application-layer event sourcing lacks durable persistence and uses conflated ID spaces — recovery fails both where infrastructure exists but is unused and where it was never built.

justifications.label: Two depth-3 conclusions spanning different architectural tiers (storage vs application) both conclude recovery is broken, but for opposite reasons — over-engineering vs under-engineering — revealing that no tier found the right calibration

no-transactional-offset-commit.text: The partitioned log provides no mechanism to atomically commit consumer offsets together with processing side effects, ruling out exactly-once delivery without external idempotency

no-vector-clocks-anywhere.text: The entire repository uses scalar Lamport clocks for ordering; no vector clock or version vector implementation exists, so true concurrency detection (distinguishing causal order from concurrent writes) is absent

none-mode-never-syncs-on-append.text: In `none` sync mode, `_do_sync()` is a complete no-op for individual appends; data reaches stable storage only via WAL rotation or explicit close

not-lehman-yao-blink-tree.text: The B-tree is a classical single-threaded B⁺-tree, not a Lehman-Yao B-link tree — internal nodes lack right-link pointers, there are no high keys, and no latch coupling; leaf sibling pointers exist solely for range scan traversal.

numa-creates-ets-access-asymmetry.text: General systems knowledge about NUMA memory architecture, not grounded in target codebase observations.

o-direct-bypasses-page-cache.text: O_DIRECT tells the kernel not to buffer the file's reads or writes in the page cache, transferring data directly between the application buffer and the storage device.

o-direct-exposes-sector-boundary-atomici.text: With O_DIRECT, a single sector-sized write is atomic from the storage device's perspective because writes go directly to the device in sector units.

o-direct-never-used.text: No storage engine in the codebase uses `O_DIRECT`; all writes go through the OS page cache.

o-direct-requires-sector-alignment.text: `O_DIRECT` requires sector-aligned writes (typically 512B or 4KB) and aligned memory buffers.

o-direct-requires-three-alignments.text: General OS/hardware constraint, not specific to this codebase; the relevant codebase fact (`no-o-direct-usage`) is already captured

offset-tracking-per-partition.text: Consumer tracks offsets as a `dict[tuple[str, int], int]` mapping `(topic, partition)` to offset, so commit granularity is per-partition, not per-message

only-new-primary-advances-view-in-vc.text: Non-primary nodes do not update `current_view` in `_handle_view_change`; they wait for the `NEW_VIEW` message to adopt the new view, leaving them in a liminal state that rejects normal-phase messages for both old and new views.

open-latest-assumes-positive-max-file-si.text: `_open_latest` assumes `_max_file_size` is positive; a zero or negative value would cause every call to fall through to `_rotate()`.

open-latest-has-toctou-window.text: `_open_latest` has a TOCTOU window between `_wal_files()` and `os.path.getsize()` if another process deletes the latest file.

open-latest-propagates-fs-errors.text: `_open_latest` does not catch filesystem errors from `os.path.getsize`, `open`, or `_rotate`; they propagate and fail WAL construction or truncation.

operation-result-tracks-partition-cost.text: Every `DocumentPartitionedDB` and `TermPartitionedDB` operation returns an `OperationResult` with a `partitions_touched` field, making read/write amplification cost observable and directly comparable between strategies.

ordering-infrastructure-broken-at-every-.text: Ordering and position infrastructure is broken or volatile at every layer: WAL sequence numbers are diligently computed and stored but never consulted during recovery, event sourcing conflates stream-scoped and global position IDs creating addressing ambiguity, and CDC consumer positions exist only in memory and are lost on restart — no ordering mechanism in the codebase reliably serves its intended purpose.

justifications.label: Three independent ordering/position mechanisms across storage, event sourcing, and CDC each fail differently (unused, conflated, volatile), revealing a systematic inability to maintain reliable ordered cursors

ordering-models-are-incompatible-across-.text: The codebase uses three incompatible time/ordering models with no unifying framework: Lamport clocks provide total order via node-ID tiebreaking, vector clocks provide partial order with explicit concurrency detection, and wall-clock timestamps provide no causal guarantees and are not even monotonic.

justifications.label: Total order, partial order, and wall-clock time coexist with no bridging abstraction

orphaned-tmp-means-original-intact.text: Describes behavior of a proposed cleanup protocol that does not exist in the codebase

orset-add-wins-semantics.text: Concurrent add and remove of the same element in `ORSet` resolves in favor of the add, because the add's unique tag was not in the remover's tombstone snapshot

metadata.example:
def merge(self, other):
    merged_tombstones = self._tombstones | other._tombstones
    merged_tags = (self_tags | other_tags) - merged_tombstones
    # new add() creates fresh tag not in tombstones -> add wins

orset-no-causal-context.text: The ORSet implementation uses no version vector, dot context, or causal summary to compress tombstone state; each removed tag is stored individually as a `(replica_id, seq)` tuple in the tombstone set

orset-remove-absent-returns-false.text: `ORSet.remove` returns `False` if the element is not present rather than raising an exception.

orset-remove-moves-tags-to-tombstones-an.text: ORSet.remove() updates _tombstones with all active tags for the element and deletes the element from _elements.

orset-remove-only-tombstones-known-tags.text: ORSet.remove only tombstones tags that are locally known, so tags added by other replicas survive a local remove and can cause the element to remain present after merge.

orset-remove-returns-false-for-absent.text: `ORSet.remove()` returns `False` for a non-existent element rather than raising an exception, treating removal of absent elements as a no-op with a boolean status indicator.

orset-tag-is-replica-id-and-sequence.text: `ORSet.add()` tags each element with a unique `(replica_id, seq_num)` pair.

orset-tombstone-growth-unbounded-and-nec.text: ORSet tombstones create an inherent resource leak: they must be retained indefinitely for merge correctness (removing them causes deleted elements to reappear when merging with replicas that still hold the original tags), yet they grow monotonically with no compaction or garbage collection, meaning memory consumption increases without bound over the set's lifetime proportional to total remove operations.

justifications.label: Merge correctness requires tombstone retention but retention without compaction creates unbounded growth

orset-tombstone-required-for-merge-corre.text: Dropping ORSet tombstones would cause removed elements to reappear when merging with a replica that still holds the element's active tags — the tombstone set in `merge()` at line 165 suppresses stale tags via set difference

orset-tombstone-set-monotonic.text: `ORSet._tombstones` is append-only: tags are added during `remove()` and unioned during `merge()` but never deleted, so the tombstone set grows without bound over the lifetime of the replica

orset-tombstones-grow-monotonically.text: `ORSet._tombstones` is only ever unioned during `merge()` and added to during `remove()`; there is no compaction or garbage collection, so the tombstone set grows without bound

overlapping-determines-merge-set.text: The merge set for leveled compaction is always exactly one source SSTable plus all SSTables in the target level whose key range intersects it, constructed via `_overlapping()` at `sstable.py:428-429`.

overlapping-is-pure-query.text: `_overlapping` performs no I/O, mutation, or side effects — it operates entirely on in-memory metadata (`min_key`, `max_key`) cached during `SSTableReader` construction.

overlapping-no-explicit-error-handling.text: `_overlapping` has no explicit error handling; it assumes every `SSTableReader` was constructed successfully and its cached metadata is valid.

overlapping-preserves-candidate-order.text: `_overlapping` returns the overlapping subset in the same order as the input `candidates` list.

overlapping-query-window-defined-by-firs.text: `_overlapping(sst, candidates)` uses the first `sst` argument's key range as the query window and tests every candidate against that window.

overlapping-single-key-sstable-matches-c.text: If the query SSTable has `min_key == max_key`, `_overlapping` still finds any candidate whose key range contains that single key.

overlapping-uses-interval-overlap-test.text: `_overlapping` determines SSTable key-range overlap using the standard interval overlap test (`a.min_key <= b.max_key AND a.max_key >= b.min_key`) with lexicographic string comparison matching the SSTable sort order.

own-deletion-hides-version.text: When version.deleted_by equals tx.tx_id, _is_visible returns False, so a transaction does not see versions it deleted itself.

own-writes-always-visible.text: A transaction always sees versions it created itself (`created_by == tx.tx_id`), regardless of commit status, ensuring read-your-own-writes consistency within a transaction.

padding-leaves-use-empty-hash.text: Non-power-of-2 leaf counts are padded with `EMPTY_HASH` (SHA-256 of empty bytes) to form a complete binary tree; these padding nodes appear in proof paths but do not represent real data.

page-header-format-is-u8-type-u16-num-ke.text: Every B-tree page starts with a 3-byte header consisting of a 1-byte page type (u8) and a 2-byte number of keys (u16), packed as `>BH`.

page-io-counters-are-resettable.text: Duplicates `btree-counters-reset-per-operation` and `iter-no-counter-reset` which already cover the counter reset behavior.

page-manager-4096-coincidence.text: `PageManager` defaults to 4096-byte pages matching the OS page size and common disk sector size, but this is a coincidental match with `O_DIRECT` alignment requirements — the implementation uses buffered I/O through Python's `open()` and never enforces alignment

page-manager-allocate-page-read-modify-w.text: PageManager.allocate_page performs an unprotected read-modify-write on the metadata page, so two concurrent callers can allocate the same page number.

page-manager-allocate-page-unprotected.text: PageManager.allocate_page performs an unprotected read-modify-write on the metadata page; two concurrent callers would allocate the same page number.

page-manager-file-growth-happens-on-writ.text: PageManager.allocate_page advances next_free without growing the file; the actual file growth happens on the subsequent write_page.

page-manager-flush-not-durable.text: PageManager calls `flush()` on every `write_page` and `_write_meta` call but only calls `os.fsync()` in `sync()` and `close()`, so individual page writes are not crash-durable without the WAL layer

page-manager-free-list-cycle-causes-infi.text: If a free-list pointer cycle exists in PageManager, allocate_page loops forever reusing the same pages.

page-manager-init-failure-leaks-file-han.text: If PageManager.__init__ fails after open() but before setup completes, the file handle is not closed.

page-manager-meta-reads-untracked.text: `read_meta()` does not increment `pages_read`, so metadata access is invisible to the I/O statistics reported by `BTree.stats`

page-manager-metadata-durability-gap.text: B-tree metadata has a durability gap at both lifecycle points: initial creation writes metadata directly without WAL protection, and all subsequent updates flush but never fsync, meaning metadata can be lost or inconsistent after any crash regardless of when it occurred.

justifications.label: Metadata is unprotected at both creation (no WAL) and update (no fsync), covering the entire lifecycle

page-manager-no-page-size-on-disk.text: The page size is not persisted in the data file; reopening with a different `page_size` value silently corrupts all page reads with no error or detection mechanism

page-manager-sync-calls-flush-and-fsync.text: In `btree.py`, `PageManager.sync()` calls `flush()` followed by `os.fsync()` to ensure data pages are durable.

page-manager-write-page-flushes-without-.text: `PageManager.write_page` flushes data to the OS page cache but does not call `os.fsync`; durability occurs only when `PageManager.sync()` or `close()` is called.

page-padding-to-page-size.text: `_wal_write_page` pads data to exactly `page_size` with null bytes before passing it to both `wal.log_write` and `pm.write_page`, ensuring the WAL record and data file page are byte-identical.

page-size-caps-keys-per-node.text: PageManager has a page_size parameter (default 4096) that physically caps how many keys fit per page.

page-size-constrains-max-keys.text: Contradicts `no-page-size-enforcement-in-serialize` — serialization does not enforce page size limits, so the constraint is not actively enforced in code.

page-size-default-is-4096.text: `PageManager` defaults to 4096-byte pages, matching typical filesystem block size; this sets the hard upper bound for serialized leaf and internal node content.

page-zero-is-metadata.text: Page 0 is always the metadata page and must never be written directly — only through `_write_meta`; user data pages start at page 1, with the initial empty leaf root always at page 1

parallel-hint-loading-requires-barrier.text: Describes Erlang startup protocol, not this Python codebase

partial-hint-load-truncates-silently.text: `_load_hint_file` in both Bitcask implementations treats a short read as end-of-file (breaks out of the read loop without error), silently dropping all keys that would have appeared after the truncation point

partial-merge-avoids-cross-level-reads.text: Describes RocksDB's MergeOperator design, not a claim about this codebase which has no merge operator implementation

participant-cannot-self-resolve.text: `Participant.recover()` returns a list of in-doubt transaction IDs but cannot commit or abort them; only the coordinator holds the decision, so participants remain locked until `Coordinator.recover()` re-sends it.

participant-recover-returns-in-doubt-tra.text: `Participant.recover()` scans its log and returns transaction IDs stuck in the `"prepared"` state as in-doubt transactions.

partition-failures-compound-across-membe.text: Network partitions create cascading failures across the membership and consensus layers: gossip-based failure detection is the single correctness gate for replication, and Raft's partition hazard (stale leader silently accepting doomed writes, forced re-election on rejoin) depends on membership accuracy that gossip's timeout-based suspicion may misjudge.

justifications.label: inaccurate membership detection feeds incorrect state to consensus, compounding both layers' partition vulnerabilities

partition-local-index-only-own-documents.text: A document-partitioned index stores each partition's local_index entries only for documents held by that same partition.

partitioned-hash-join-partitions-both-si.text: `PartitionedHashJoin.join()` calls `partition_dataset()` on both inputs before joining, meaning partitions are computed at join time rather than assumed from storage layout

partitioned-log-auto-commit-after-nonemp.text: When auto_commit is enabled, Consumer.poll commits offsets after every non-empty poll.

partitioned-log-committed-offset-resumes.text: A new consumer in the same group resumes from the last committed offset after the previous consumer partially consumes with max_messages=3, commits, and closes.

partitioned-log-compaction-preserves-key.text: Log compaction retains only the last occurrence per key but always preserves messages with `key=None`.

partitioned-log-group-assignment-complet.text: Consumer group partition assignment forms a complete, non-overlapping partition of all topic partitions across group members.

partitioned-log-idle-consumers-when-grou.text: With 1 partition and 3 consumers in a group, exactly 2 consumers are idle with empty assignments.

partitioned-log-key-routing-deterministi.text: Messages with the same key always route to the same partition via `MD5(key) % num_partitions`, guaranteeing per-key ordering within a partition.

metadata.example:
def _partition_for_key(self, key):
    return hash(key) % self._num_partitions

partitioned-log-offset-monotonic.text: Offsets within a partition are strictly increasing and never reused; `_base_offsets` only advances forward via `truncate` and `compact_partition`.

partitioned-log-partition-count-limit.text: `Topic.__init__` enforces partition count between 1 and 128, raising `ValueError` outside that range.

partitioned-log-persistence-jsonl.text: When `persist_dir` is set, messages are appended as JSONL files named `{topic}_{partition}.jsonl` and committed offsets are written to a single `offsets.json`.

partitioned-log-poll-advances-position.text: Consumer.poll() advances the consumer's internal offset so a second poll with no new messages returns an empty list.

partitioned-log-producer-partition-resol.text: Producer.send resolves a partition by explicit partition first, then MD5 key hash mod partition count, then per-topic round-robin for keyless messages.

partitioned-log-rebalance-eager-round-ro.text: `ConsumerGroup.rebalance()` is synchronous and triggered on every membership change, distributing partitions round-robin across sorted consumer IDs — no incremental or cooperative protocol.

partitioned-log-retention-size-based.text: Broker.enforce_retention truncates a partition from the head when the partition exceeds max_log_size.

partitioned-log-retention-time-based.text: Broker.enforce_retention truncates messages older than retention_ms when retention_ms > 0.

partitioned-log-round-robin-even-distrib.text: Round-robin routing distributes 9 keyless messages evenly across 3 partitions as [3,3,3].

partitioned-log-topic-append-assigns-nex.text: Topic.append assigns the next partition offset and stamps the Message with topic, partition, and offset.

partitioned-log-truncate-advances-base-o.text: Topic.truncate removes count messages from the head of a partition and advances _base_offsets to preserve offset continuity.

payload-only-crc-leaves-metadata-unprote.text: All three storage engine WAL implementations share a systematic integrity blind spot: CRC checksums cover only data payloads, leaving routing metadata (sequence numbers, page numbers) unprotected against silent corruption.

justifications.label: Three independent observations converge on the same architectural gap — metadata fields that control WHERE data is applied are never integrity-checked

pbft-check-prepared-invalid-state-return.text: `_check_prepared` returns an empty list without raising exceptions when the prepared predicate is not satisfied or state is invalid.

pbft-check-prepared-returns-own-commit-a.text: `_check_prepared` returns its own COMMIT message plus any messages produced by `_check_committed` when the commit threshold is also crossed.

pbft-client-acceptance-requires-f-plus-1.text: The PBFT test suite requires at least `f+1` matching replies for client acceptance.

pbft-cluster-validates-n-3f-plus-1.text: `PBFTCluster` raises `ValueError` if `n` is not exactly `3f+1` or if more than `f` byzantine nodes are specified, enforcing the minimum redundancy required for Byzantine fault tolerance.

pbft-commit-self-logged-before-broadcast.text: `_check_prepared` logs the node's own COMMIT into `message_log` and `phase_senders` before returning it for broadcast, so duplicate detection correctly rejects re-delivery of the node's own COMMIT.

pbft-default-str-fragile.text: The `default=str` parameter in the PBFT digest function silently converts non-serializable objects to their `str()` representation, which is not deterministic across replicas for types like `datetime` or custom objects — a latent consensus-breaking bug if non-primitive request payloads are introduced.

pbft-duplicate-messages-silently-dropped.text: `PBFTNode.receive_message` returns an empty list for duplicate or invalid messages (out-of-range sender IDs, already-seen tuples) rather than raising exceptions, consistent with Byzantine protocol design where you can't trust the sender.

pbft-executed-log-sequence-numbers-conti.text: Honest nodes execute requests with contiguous sequence numbers starting from 1, enforced by the protocol's ordering guarantees and verified by test assertions on the `_executed_log`.

pbft-new-primary-selected-by-view-modulo.text: In `_handle_view_change`, the new primary for a target view is determined by `target_view % total_nodes`.

pbft-prepare-digest-match-required.text: Duplicates existing belief `wrong-digest-cannot-reach-quorum` which already captures that mismatched digests are silently dropped and cannot contribute to quorum.

pbft-prepared-at-most-once.text: A `(view, seq)` pair can transition to "prepared" at most once per node, enforced by the `prepared_requests` set guard at the top of `_check_prepared`.

pbft-prepared-chains-to-committed.text: `_check_prepared` always calls `_check_committed` after marking prepared, enabling immediate commit if enough COMMIT messages arrived out of order before the node reached the prepared state.

pbft-prepared-threshold-is-2f.text: `_check_prepared` requires exactly 2f matching PREPAREs (not 2f+1) because the primary's PRE-PREPARE counts as implicit agreement toward the quorum of 2f+1.

pbft-primary-skips-prepare.text: The primary sends PRE-PREPARE but not PREPARE; `_handle_prepare` rejects PREPAREs from the primary, and the primary's code path in `_handle_pre_prepare` skips sending a PREPARE — this asymmetry is why the prepared threshold is 2f not 2f+1.

pbft-quorum-thresholds-2f-and-2f1.text: PBFT prepare quorum requires 2f matching PREPARE messages, while commit quorum requires 2f+1 matching COMMIT messages.

pbft-run-protocol-bounded-rounds.text: `PBFTCluster.run_protocol(max_rounds)` delivers pending messages for a bounded number of rounds.

pbft-sole-sort-keys-user.text: `byzantine-fault-tolerance/pbft.py:46` is the only call site in the codebase that uses `json.dumps(sort_keys=True)` for hashing; all other `json.dumps` calls are for storage serialization where canonical form is irrelevant.

pbft-submit-request-is-synchronous-simul.text: `PBFTCluster.submit_request` runs the full three-phase protocol to completion deterministically in a single call (no real networking or async), returning a boolean success indicator.

pbft-trigger-view-change-returns-new-vie.text: `PBFTCluster.trigger_view_change()` forces a view change and returns the new view number.

pbft-verify-agreement-checks-identical-h.text: `PBFTCluster.verify_agreement()` checks that all honest nodes have identical executed logs.

pbft-view-change-dedup-by-sender.text: `_handle_view_change` records at most one VIEW_CHANGE message per sender per target view in `view_change_msgs`, preventing ballot stuffing by Byzantine nodes.

pbft-view-change-malformed-prepared-rais.text: `_handle_view_change` assumes each `msg.data["prepared"]` entry has `sequence`, `request`, `digest`, and `view` keys, so a malformed entry raises `KeyError`.

pbft-view-change-new-primary-resets-time.text: When the new primary advances to `target_view`, `_handle_view_change` resets `timer_ms` to 0.

pbft-view-change-preserves-prepared-requ.text: Requests that reach the prepared state survive view changes: the new primary collects prepared-but-uncommitted requests from VIEW_CHANGE messages and re-proposes them with fresh PRE_PREPARE messages in the new view.

pbft-view-change-preserves-safety-and-li.text: PBFT view changes maintain both safety (requiring 2f+1 messages before acting) and liveness (carrying prepared-but-uncommitted requests into the new view), matching the theoretical protocol guarantees.

justifications.label: Two independent observations confirm that the implementation correctly handles both halves of the view-change correctness argument

pbft-view-change-safety-holds-with-stabl.text: PBFT view changes maintain safety (2f+1 agreement) and liveness (carrying prepared requests forward with contiguous sequence numbers into the new view), ensuring no committed request is lost across leader transitions.

justifications.label: The fragile default=str digest function could cause honest nodes to compute different digests for identical requests, breaking prepared certificate matching and undermining the 2f+1 threshold

pending-queue-drives-ring-propagation.text: Every accepted remote change (including synthesized merge results) is appended to `_pending` for downstream propagation, enabling multi-hop replication in ring topologies where a single sync round cannot reach all nodes.

pending-requeue-enables-multihop.text: Every accepted remote change in `apply_remote_change` is appended to `_pending`, causing it to be forwarded to the next node in the replication topology during the next sync cycle

per-record-crc-cannot-detect-reordering.text: Independent per-record CRCs in `wal.py`, `btree.py`, and `bitcask.py` validate each record in isolation, so record deletion, reordering, or splicing produces a file where every CRC passes but the log is semantically corrupt

persist-after-memory.text: The event is appended to `self._events` (in-memory) before `_persist_event` writes it to disk; a disk write failure leaves the in-memory store ahead of the on-disk log with no rollback.

persist-before-notify.text: Disk persistence via `_persist_event` happens before subscriber notification: an event is written to the NDJSON file before any `LiveProjection` or other subscriber sees it.

persist-event-append-mode-creates-missin.text: `_persist_event` opens the persist path in append mode, which creates the file if it does not already exist.

persist-event-callers-gate-on-persist-pa.text: `_persist_event` itself does not check `self._persist_path`; every caller gates on `if self._persist_path:` before calling it.

persist-event-no-fsync.text: `_persist_event` writes to the OS buffer via `file.write()` but never calls `fsync`; event data can be lost on crash between write and OS flush to disk.

persist-event-per-call-open.text: The persist file is opened in append mode and closed on every single `_persist_event` call, not held open across the store's lifetime — safe but incurs per-event open/close overhead.

persist-event-propagates-io-errors.text: `_persist_event` has no exception handling; file-open or write errors propagate uncaught to `append` or `append_batch` callers.

persist-event-serializes-timestamp-via-i.text: `_persist_event` converts the event timestamp from a `datetime` object to an ISO-8601 string via `.isoformat()` before JSON serialization.

phi-accrual-allows-per-caller-conviction.text: Phi accrual allows different callers to act at different φ conviction thresholds (for example gossip at φ > 8 and read repair at φ > 5), unlike the fixed-threshold model's single t_suspect.

phi-accrual-computes-phi-from-cdf-surviv.text: Phi accrual failure detection computes φ = -log10(1 - CDF(elapsed_time_since_last_heartbeat)), where CDF is the cumulative distribution of observed heartbeat inter-arrival times.

pipeline-add-stage-returns-self.text: `Pipeline.add_stage()` returns `self`, enabling fluent builder-style chaining of stages.

pipeline-build-iterator-special-cases-re.text: `Pipeline._build_iterator` special-cases the first stage: if it's a `ReadLines`, it uses its own source; otherwise, if `input_data` is provided, a temporary `ReadLines` is prepended but not added to `self._stages`.

pipeline-exposes-three-execution-modes.text: `pipeline.py` exposes `run()`, `run_lazy()`, and `run_to_file()` as three execution modes for materializing output, piping it, or redirecting to a file.

pipeline-imports-only-stdlib.text: `pipeline.py` imports only Python standard library modules, including `heapq`, `json`, `tempfile`, `os`, `re`, `time`, and `collections.defaultdict`.

pipeline-lazy-pull-model.text: Pipeline execution is pull-based via nested Python generators; records flow only when the terminal consumer iterates, and stages interleave execution without threads

pipeline-no-inter-stage-schema-validatio.text: Pipeline stages pass untyped tuples with no validation that the output shape of one stage matches the input expectations of the next; a mismatched stage composition fails at runtime, not at construction time

pipeline-records-are-tuples.text: Pipeline stages produce and consume lists of `(key, value)` tuples, where key is a string and value depends on the stage (string for Tokenize, int for Count).

pipeline-run-returns-list.text: `Pipeline.run()` materializes all output records into a `list`, while `run_lazy()` returns an iterator that yields records on demand without full materialization.

pipeline-run-to-file-streams-jsonl.text: `Pipeline.run_to_file()` streams results to a JSONL file without holding all records in memory.

pipeline-sort-cleanup-in-finally.text: `Sort.process` uses a `try/finally` block to delete chunk files and the temp directory even on error.

pipeline-stages-hide-materialization-bar.text: Pipeline stages have fundamentally different resource profiles hidden behind a uniform tuple interface: Count is an unbounded memory barrier that materializes all input before emitting any output, Sort bounds memory via external merge-sort disk spillover, yet both produce and consume identical tuple lists with no way for the pipeline to distinguish streaming stages from blocking ones.

justifications.label: Uniform tuple interface hides asymmetric blocking and memory characteristics

pipeline-stats-tracks-all-stages.text: Minor feature detail rather than an invariant; violating it would not break pipeline correctness

pncounter-composed-of-two-gcounters.text: PNCounter state is structured as two GCounter sub-counters (`p` for increments, `n` for decrements) with `value() = p - n`, confirming the standard decomposition from CRDT literature.

pncounter-composes-gcounters.text: `PNCounter` delegates entirely to two `GCounter` instances (`p` for increments, `n` for decrements); it contains no independent merge or counting logic

pncounter-supports-negative-values.text: PNCounter permits negative values; decrementing below zero is valid in its test suite.

pncounter-value-is-positive-minus-negati.text: `PNCounter.value()` returns `p.value() - n.value()`, where `p` and `n` are `GCounter` instances.

point-lookup-always-reaches-leaf.text: Every `get` must descend to a leaf node regardless of tree height since internal nodes hold no values; cost is exactly *h* page reads for a tree of height *h*

posix-durable-file-creation-requires-par.text: POSIX durability for creating or replacing a file requires writing data, fsyncing the file, and fsyncing the parent directory to persist the name-to-inode mapping.

posix-fsync-fdatasync-metadata-scope.text: POSIX fsync flushes file data and all file metadata, while fdatasync flushes file data and only the metadata needed to retrieve the data.

posix-fsync-is-per-file-not-cross-file.text: General POSIX specification knowledge, not a testable claim about this codebase; the cross-file ordering consequence is already captured by `btree-wal-before-data` and related beliefs.

posix-rename-is-atomic.text: POSIX `os.rename()` updates directory entries in a single atomic operation so concurrent readers see either the old name or the new name, never a torn state.

posix-rename-is-atomic-not-durable.text: POSIX `os.rename()` is atomic but does not by itself make the directory-entry change durable across a crash without fsyncing the parent directory.

posix-write-atomicity-is-concurrent-only.text: POSIX guarantees that `write()` on a regular file is atomic with respect to other reads and writes on the same file descriptor, but does not guarantee that bytes land on disk as an all-or-nothing unit.

posix-write-not-atomic-for-arbitrary-siz.text: POSIX write() is not atomic for arbitrarily sized buffers; the OS and disk can commit data in sector-sized chunks (typically 512B or 4KB).

post-crash-compaction-produces-irrecover.text: A crash during compaction produces irrecoverable data loss: no implementation uses write-temp/fsync/rename for atomicity (Bitcask deletes before renaming, LSM lacks atomic rename), and the resulting file corruption is terminal because every reader halts at the first CRC failure with no resync or skip capability.

justifications.label: non-atomic compaction + terminal corruption handling = crash during compaction is unrecoverable

postgres-defers-btree-rebalancing-to-vac.text: PostgreSQL's `nbtree` never merges or redistributes siblings on delete; it marks tuples dead and relies on VACUUM to reclaim space, trading immediate space efficiency for throughput under concurrency

postgres-nbtree-defers-rebalancing-to-va.text: PostgreSQL nbtree marks deleted index tuples as dead and defers space reclamation to VACUUM; it does not merge pages with siblings.

postgres-nbtree-half-dead-flag-enables-r.text: If a crash occurs between PostgreSQL's half-dead marking and sibling unlink phases, the durable half-dead flag lets recovery identify and finish the page deletion.

postgres-nbtree-half-dead-page-preserves.text: PostgreSQL's half-dead phase preserves the page's content while removing the parent downlink, so a scan following a sibling link can detect the half-dead flag and skip it.

postgres-nbtree-incomplete-split-repaire.text: PostgreSQL nbtree repairs an incomplete split cooperatively: a later inserter that encounters the incomplete split finishes it before proceeding.

postgres-nbtree-pagedel-and-unlink-are-s.text: PostgreSQL's _bt_pagedel marks a page half-dead in one WAL-logged operation, and _bt_unlink_halfdead_page removes it from the sibling chain in a separate WAL-logged operation.

postgres-nbtree-phase2-deletion-often-ru.text: PostgreSQL's second page-deletion phase is often run by VACUUM rather than by the original deleter.

postgres-nbtree-recycles-pages-into-free.text: PostgreSQL recycles deleted pages into a free space map rather than merging them with siblings.

postgres-nbtree-removes-empty-pages-via-.text: PostgreSQL's nbtree removes an empty page through a "half-dead" → "dead" state machine.

postgres-nbtree-uses-right-links-and-hig.text: PostgreSQL nbtree uses right-link pointers and high keys on pages so readers can descend without holding parent latches and detect concurrent splits.

postgresql-added-crc32c-in-9-5-with-wal-.text: PostgreSQL added CRC-32C in version 9.5 with a WAL format version bump.

postgresql-group-commit-uses-leader-fsyn.text: PostgreSQL's group commit coordinates concurrent waiters by having a leader transaction collect pending commit requests and perform a single `fsync` covering all of them.

postgresql-wal-segment-recycling-uses-re.text: PostgreSQL recycles old WAL segment files using `os.rename()`, which is atomic on POSIX, rather than rewriting segments in place.

predicate-exceptions-silently-skipped.text: If the predicate function throws on a `(key, value)` pair in `read_predicate`, that pair is silently excluded from results via bare `except Exception: pass` — no logging, no error propagation

premature-tombstone-removal-causes-data-.text: General correctness principle already covered by existing belief `tombstone-removal-requires-full-key-coverage`

primary-key-reads-unaffected-by-async.text: `get(pk)` reads directly from `partitions[pid].documents` and is never affected by `async_index` mode — staleness only applies to `query_by_field` which reads from `global_index`

producer-keyed-hash-unkeyed-roundrobin.text: Partitioned log `Producer` hashes keyed messages to a fixed partition for ordering guarantees, and round-robins unkeyed messages across partitions for load distribution

production-btree-min-fill-half-full.text: Production B+ trees require every non-root node to be at least half full, i.e. at least `ceil(m/2)` keys for order `m`.

production-btrees-split-on-byte-fullness.text: Production B-trees such as InnoDB and SQLite split pages based on byte fullness rather than a fixed key count.

production-lcs-picks-least-overlap-to-mi.text: Production leveled compaction systems such as Cassandra and RocksDB pick the SSTable with the least overlap with the next level to minimize bytes rewritten per compaction and thereby reduce write amplification.

projection-auto-snapshot-interval.text: When a Projection is constructed with snapshot_interval, catch_up() automatically calls save_snapshot() after that many events and resets its since-snapshot counter.

projection-auto-snapshots-after-interval.text: The `_snapshot_interval` parameter causes a projection to automatically snapshot after processing N events.

projection-catch-up-advances-position-fo.text: `catch_up` advances `_position` for every event, not just those with registered handlers, so unhandled event types don't create replay gaps

projection-catch-up-assumes-sequential-i.text: `catch_up` uses `from_position=self._position + 1` arithmetic that assumes `event_id` values are contiguous integers with no gaps; IDs with gaps would cause events to be silently skipped

projection-catch-up-poison-event-stalls.text: If a handler raises during `catch_up`, `_position` is not advanced past the failing event, causing all subsequent `catch_up` calls to re-encounter and re-fail on the same event indefinitely

projection-is-stateless-replay.text: A `Projection`'s `_state` is a cache of derived data, not a source of truth — it can be fully reconstructed from the event log at any time by replaying from position 0

projection-snapshot-interval-counts-all-.text: The snapshot interval counter increments for every event processed during `catch_up`, including those without handlers, so snapshot frequency is based on total event throughput not just handled events

protocol-safety-unfalsifiable-under-curr.text: Distributed protocol safety claims are unfalsifiable under the current testing methodology: specific protocol gaps (2PC's blocking window with unused timeout, Raft's stale-leader writes) AND general protocol behavior are validated exclusively under synchronous simulation with deterministic delivery — safety violations that manifest only under asynchronous or partitioned delivery are structurally invisible to the test suite.

justifications.label: Synchronous-only testing masks safety gaps that require asynchronous delivery to manifest

protocol-safety-validated-only-under-syn.text: Distributed protocol safety properties are validated exclusively under synchronous simulation (deterministic tick-based delivery, no real network I/O), but the most critical failure mode — network partitions creating stale-leader write acceptance and forced re-elections — is inherently asynchronous, creating an untested gap between modeled and real-world safety.

justifications.label: Partition hazards are modeled but only tested under instant delivery — async timing effects remain unvalidated

put-append-only.text: `put` never modifies existing on-disk data; overwrites create a new record appended to the active segment and update only the in-memory index, leaving old records as reclaimable garbage until compaction

put-crash-recovery-gap.text: The crash window between `_write_record` and index update is already covered by `bitcask-partial-write-safe` and `bitcask-crash-recovery-without-hints`

put-no-tombstone-guard.text: `put` does not reject the `TOMBSTONE` sentinel as a value; passing it creates a record indistinguishable from a delete, which silently corrupts the key's state on recovery

put-not-thread-safe.text: Covered by existing `no-concurrency-primitives` which applies to the entire codebase

put-return-value-ignored-by-coordinator.text: `ReadRepairStore` never checks the boolean return from `Replica.put()` during read repair or writes, relying on version monotonicity to make stale or redundant writes harmless no-ops.

put-size-validation-checks-single-entry-.text: `BTree.put`'s size check verifies only that the new entry would fit in an otherwise empty leaf; it does not account for existing entries in the target leaf.

put-triggers-compaction.text: Substantially overlaps with existing `bitcask-auto-compact-threshold` which already captures the auto-compaction trigger behavior

pyc-pattern-is-redundant-on-py3.text: Trivia about Python internals; doesn't affect how developers work in the codebase

pytest-files-have-broader-coverage.text: The `test_*.py` files are consistently longer than their `tester_test_*.py` counterparts (e.g., 207 vs 125 lines for bloom-filter), containing additional edge case tests beyond the tester's core invariant checks

pytest-files-have-no-main-guard.text: The `test_*.py` files contain no `if __name__` blocks, so they are designed exclusively to run via pytest.

pytest-files-rely-on-pytest-runner.text: The `test_*.py` files import pytest and use bare `assert` statements, relying on pytest for discovery, execution, and reporting.

pytest-must-run-per-directory.text: Tests must be executed from within each module's directory (e.g., `cd bloom-filter && pytest`) because imports use bare module names with no package prefix or installed package

python-bitcask-lacks-atomic-keydir-swap.text: Both Python Bitcask implementations mutate the keydir dict directly in place with no atomic swap or generation concept, unlike Erlang Bitcask's ETS table swap.

python-bitcask-no-keydir-sharing.text: Each `BitcaskStore` instance independently rebuilds the full in-memory index from disk; there is no shared-memory mechanism to preserve or share the keydir across instances even within the same process, unlike Erlang's ETS-backed keydir

python-bitcask-no-refcount-or-locking.text: Neither Python Bitcask implementation has reference counting, reader registration, or file-handle locking — compaction can delete segment files while a concurrent reader holds a stale index entry, unlike Erlang Bitcask which defers deletion until the last reader's refcount drops to zero.

python-bitcask-single-threaded-scope.text: Intent/opinion claim ("deliberate scope boundary, not a bug"); the technical fact is already captured by `compact-single-threaded-assumption`.

python-bytes-never-page-aligned.text: General CPython runtime implementation detail, not a testable claim about this codebase

python-crc32c-package-auto-detects-hardw.text: The Python `crc32c` package auto-detects and uses hardware SSE4.2 or ARM CRC instructions when available.

python-flush-only-reaches-page-cache.text: Python file.flush() only pushes data into the OS page cache; os.fsync(fd) is required to force dirty pages to durable storage.

python-open-allocates-unaligned-buffers.text: General CPython runtime behavior, not a testable claim about this codebase

quorum-guarantees-weakened-at-two-levels.text: The distributed storage layer systematically weakens quorum semantics: sloppy quorums count hint storage as successful writes, and sub-quorum configurations (R+W<=N) produce only warnings rather than errors, making it possible to operate without intersection guarantees.

justifications.label: Two independent weakening mechanisms stack — hints inflate write-quorum counts while the safety check is advisory-only

quorum-violation-warns-not-raises.text: When `R + W <= N`, the `ReadRepairStore` constructor emits a `warnings.warn` rather than raising an exception, allowing intentionally relaxed quorum configurations.

raft-advance-commit-leader-guard-at-call.text: Both call sites of _advance_commit_index verify self._state == 'leader' before invoking it.

raft-advance-commit-no-early-exit.text: raft._advance_commit_index continues scanning after finding a committable index so _commit_index ends at the highest majority-replicated current-term entry.

raft-advance-commit-on-tick-and-response.text: `_advance_commit_index` is invoked both on heartbeat ticks and immediately after successful append responses update `_match_index`, allowing eager commit advancement without waiting for the next heartbeat cycle.

raft-append-mismatch-returns-match-index.text: `handle_append_entries` returns `success=False` with the follower's current `match_index` on a log mismatch, which the leader uses to back up `next_index` and retry.

raft-cluster-deterministic-simulation.text: `RaftCluster` uses tick-based deterministic simulation with no real clocks, threads, or network I/O; time advances only via explicit `tick(ms)` calls, making partition and election scenarios fully reproducible.

raft-commit-index-monotonic.text: `_commit_index` only ever increases within `_advance_commit_index` because the loop starts at `_commit_index + 1` and only assigns forward; it can never decrease or be reset.

raft-commit-requires-strict-majority.text: An entry is committed when `count > total // 2`, meaning for a 5-node cluster at least 3 replicas (including the leader) must have the entry, matching Raft's quorum requirement.

raft-committed-data-survives-consecutive.text: `test_sequential_leader_failures` verifies that committed data survives two consecutive leader failures.

raft-committed-entries-exclude-sentinel.text: `get_committed_entries()` returns log entries at or below `_commit_index` and excludes the sentinel entry at index 0.

raft-current-term-commit-only.text: `_advance_commit_index` only commits entries whose term matches `_current_term`, implementing the Raft safety property from §5.4.2 that prevents committing prior-term entries by replica count alone.

metadata.example:
if self._log[n].term != self._current_term:
    continue  # only commit entries from current term

raft-follower-commit-min-leader-commit-l.text: On the follower side, handle_append_entries sets the commit index to min(leader_commit, last_log_index).

raft-follower-rejects-writes.text: `RaftNode.client_request()` on a follower returns `{"success": False, "error": "not leader"}` as a structured dict rather than raising an exception; only the leader accepts client writes.

raft-healed-follower-catches-up-on-misse.text: `test_heal_and_log_consistency` verifies that a healed follower catches up on log entries it missed during a partition.

raft-heartbeat-keeps-leader-stable-100-t.text: `test_heartbeat_prevents_elections` verifies that heartbeats keep the elected leader and term stable across 100 ticks.

raft-is-multi-paxos-optimization.text: The Raft implementation in `raft-consensus/raft.py` embodies the Multi-Paxos leader-lease pattern: one election per term via `_become_leader`, then Phase-2-only replication (AppendEntries) for all entries within that term — heartbeats act as the lease

raft-log-direct-indexed.text: Log entries are accessed by log index as a direct Python list index (`self._log[prev_log_index]`), which assumes all entries from index 0 onward are present — log truncation would require an offset or a different data structure

raft-log-never-shrinks.text: `self._log` in `RaftNode` is append-only: no method ever removes entries, so the log grows monotonically with client requests and memory usage is unbounded

raft-log-sentinel-index-zero.text: raft.py's log is indexed from a sentinel at position 0.

raft-match-index-defaults-zero.text: Peers missing from `_match_index` are treated as having replicated nothing via `dict.get(peer, 0)`; `_become_leader` initializes all peers to 0, so this default is safe but allows graceful handling of unexpected state.

raft-minority-cannot-elect.text: A partition containing fewer than a strict majority of nodes cannot elect a leader; `get_leader()` returns `None` for a 2-of-5 minority partition.

raft-no-leader-forwarding.text: `client_request` returns `{"success": False, "error": "not leader"}` if the node is not the leader; there is no automatic forwarding to the current leader.

raft-no-prevote-or-lease.text: The Raft implementation has no PreVote, leader lease, or CheckQuorum mechanism; split-brain safety relies entirely on term numbers and the single-vote-per-term invariant

raft-no-state-machine-apply.text: `_last_applied` is tracked but never used to actually apply commands to a state machine, making snapshotting impossible without first implementing application logic

raft-nodes-start-as-followers-term-zero.text: `test_all_nodes_start_as_followers` asserts that every node begins in the follower role with `current_term == 0`.

raft-partition-creates-dual-hazard.text: Network partitions create a compound safety hazard in Raft: the isolated leader silently accepts writes that can never commit, and when it rejoins its inflated term forces a disruptive re-election of the healthy partition's leader.

justifications.label: Two partition-related behaviors combine into a scenario where partitions cause both silent data loss AND unnecessary leader disruption on heal

raft-partition-via-set.text: Network partitions are simulated by adding node IDs to `_partitioned`; partitioned nodes neither tick nor send/receive messages, modeling complete network isolation.

metadata.example:
self._partitioned = set()
# ...
if sender in self._partitioned or receiver in self._partitioned:
    continue  # drop message

raft-randomized-timeout-only-split-vote-.text: The only mechanism preventing simultaneous candidacy is the randomized election timeout range (default 150–300ms); there is no protocol-level tiebreaker such as PreVote

raft-rejoin-forces-election.text: A partitioned node that rejoins after repeated failed elections carries an inflated term number, forcing the healthy leader to step down via `_become_follower` and triggering a completely unnecessary cluster-wide election

raft-sentinel-entry-assumption.text: The Raft log is initialized with a sentinel `LogEntry(term=0, index=0, command=None)` at position 0, and multiple methods depend on this entry always being present at `self._log[0]`

raft-sentinel-log-entry.text: The log is initialized with a sentinel `LogEntry(term=0, index=0)` at position 0 that is never removed, eliminating empty-log edge cases in `_last_log_index()` and `_last_log_term()`.

metadata.example: self._log = [LogEntry(term=0, index=0, command=None)]  # sentinel

raft-single-tick-delivery.text: `RaftCluster.tick()` collects outbound messages and delivers both the request and its response within the same tick invocation — there is no simulated network latency.

raft-split-vote-test-seeds-random-and-na.text: `test_split_vote_resolves` sets `random.seed(42)` and uses an election timeout range of `(150, 155)` ms to provoke split votes deterministically.

raft-stale-leader-accepts-writes.text: A partitioned leader continues accepting client requests (returning `success: True`) even though those entries can never commit and will be overwritten when the partition heals — the gap a leader lease would close

raft-state-persistent-volatile-leader-on.text: `RaftNode` separates state into persistent (`_current_term`, `_voted_for`, `_log`), volatile (`_state`, `_commit_index`, `_last_applied`), and leader-only (`_next_index`, `_match_index`) categories.

raft-step-down-on-higher-term-rpc.text: Every Raft RPC handler calls `_become_follower(term)` when the incoming term is greater than `_current_term`.

raft-terms-strictly-increase.text: Each new leader election produces a strictly higher term than the previous leader; terms never repeat or decrease across leader transitions, as validated by the `test_terms_monotonically_increasing` test.

raft-tests-use-cluster-facade-not-node-m.text: The Raft test suite drives protocol behavior through `RaftCluster` methods (`run_until_leader`, `submit`, `run_until_committed`, `partition_node`, `heal_node`, `get_committed_log`) rather than calling `RaftNode` protocol methods directly.

raft-uncommitted-entries-overwritten.text: Uncommitted log entries from a deposed leader are overwritten when the node receives `AppendEntries` from a new leader with conflicting entries at the same index; only committed entries are durable.

raft-vote-granted-requires-up-to-date-lo.text: `handle_request_vote` grants a vote only if the voter has not voted in the term (or already voted for the candidate) and the candidate's log is at least as up-to-date by comparing term first, then index.

range-partition-contains-key-tests-range.text: `Partition.contains_key(key)` returns `True` if the key lies in the partition's `[start_key, end_key)` range regardless of whether data exists for that key.

range-partition-delete-is-o-n-pop.text: `Partition.delete` removes a key with an O(n) list pop and returns a boolean indicating whether the key existed.

range-partition-delete-then-merge-preser.text: `test_delete_then_merge` verifies that bulk deletion followed by `merge_small_partitions()` consolidates partitions while surviving keys remain accessible.

range-partition-get-is-o-log-n.text: `Partition.get` performs an O(log n) binary search lookup.

range-partition-large-scale-test-verifie.text: `test_large_scale_balanced` inserts 10,000 keys and asserts that no partition exceeds `max_partition_size`, boundaries stay contiguous, and the total key count is preserved.

range-partition-merge-guards-threshold.text: `merge_small_partitions()` only merges adjacent partitions when their combined size stays below `min_partition_size`, preventing immediate re-splitting after merge.

range-partition-merge-is-greedy-left-to-.text: `merge_small_partitions` sweeps left-to-right and greedily merges adjacent pairs whose combined size is at or below `min_partition_size`, which can produce different results than an optimal merge strategy

range-partition-merge-rechecks-same-inde.text: After merging two adjacent partitions, `merge_small_partitions()` re-checks the same index without incrementing `i`, allowing cascading merges.

range-partition-no-exceptions-api.text: `RangePartitionedStore` uses return-value signaling: `get()` returns `None` for missing keys and `delete()` returns `False` for absent keys, rather than raising exceptions.

range-partition-owns-half-open-interval.text: Each `Partition` in `range_partitioning.py` owns a half-open key interval `[start_key, end_key)`.

range-partition-put-uses-bisect-left-o-n.text: `Partition.put` uses `bisect_left` to find the sorted insertion point and then performs O(n) list insertion while maintaining sorted key order.

range-partition-routing-after-splits-ret.text: `test_routing_after_splits` verifies that `get_partition_for_key` returns the correct partition metadata for each key after splits.

range-partition-sequential-insert-skew.text: Range partitioning has its own skew risk: keys arriving in sorted order all hit the rightmost partition; `Partition.split()` mitigates this for data already stored by splitting at the median, but cannot prevent temporary hotspots during sequential ingestion

range-partition-split-at-median.text: `Partition.split` always divides at the median key (index `len // 2`), which can produce uneven partitions when key distribution is skewed

range-partition-split-empty-raises-index.text: Calling `Partition.split()` on an empty partition raises `IndexError` because it indexes `_keys[len(_keys)//2]` without checking for emptiness.

range-partition-store-scan-handles-end-b.text: `RangePartitionedStore.range_scan` special-cases an `end_key` that exactly matches a partition boundary to avoid including an empty scan of the next partition.

range-partition-update-does-not-change-t.text: `test_update_value` verifies that overwriting an existing key with `put` updates the value without changing `total_keys`.

range-partitioning-auto-split-manual-mer.text: Splits are triggered automatically during `put()` when a partition exceeds `max_partition_size`, but merges require an explicit call to `merge_small_partitions()` and never happen implicitly.

range-partitioning-boundary-routing-bise.text: Key routing uses `bisect_right(boundaries, key) - 1` on a parallel sorted list of partition start keys, giving O(log p) partition lookup where p is the partition count.

range-partitioning-contiguous-half-open-.text: Partitions use half-open intervals `[start_key, end_key)` with the first partition starting at `""` and the last having `end_key=None`, guaranteeing the entire string keyspace is covered with no gaps or overlaps.

range-partitioning-merge-assumes-adjacen.text: `Partition.merge(other)` appends the other partition's keys without re-sorting; correctness depends on the caller passing the immediate right neighbor, with no runtime adjacency validation.

range-partitioning-no-thread-safety.text: No concurrency protection exists on any mutation path (`put`, `delete`, `split`, `merge`); concurrent access would corrupt the sorted key/value lists.

range-partitioning-parallel-arrays-routi.text: `_partitions` and `_boundaries` are kept in lockstep as parallel arrays — index `i` in both refers to the same partition — trading O(n) insert/delete for O(1) indexed access and O(log n) binary search routing.

range-partitioning-routing-is-structural.text: Range partitioning routing depends on maintaining strict lockstep invariants across parallel data structures that are never verified: boundaries and partitions are kept as parallel arrays where any desynchronization silently misroutes keys, merge operations assume partition adjacency without checking, and splits always divide at the median regardless of key distribution skew.

justifications.label: Parallel array coupling and unverified adjacency assumptions make routing fragile

range-partitioning-split-at-median-index.text: `Partition.split()` divides at `len(keys)//2` (count-based median), not the lexicographic midpoint of the key range, producing equal-count halves but potentially unequal key ranges.

metadata.example:
mid = len(partition._data) // 2
median_key = sorted_keys[mid]
# split into [start, median) and [median, end)

range-scan-all-tombstoned-returns-empty.text: If every matching key in the range has been tombstoned, `range_scan` returns an empty list, making the result indistinguishable from no keys in range.

range-scan-assumes-string-keys.text: `range_scan` assumes both `start_key` and `end_key` are strings; comparing a non-string key to the stored string keys produces undefined behavior.

range-scan-complexity-log-n-plus-k.text: `Partition.range_scan` runs in O(log n) for the two binary searches plus O(k) to materialize k result pairs.

range-scan-end-key-exclusive.text: `range_scan(start_key, end_key)` treats `end_key` as an exclusive upper bound — `range_scan("k05", "k10")` returns keys `k05` through `k09`

range-scan-exceptions-propagate.text: `range_scan` has no explicit error handling; `FileNotFoundError`, `IOError`, and `UnicodeDecodeError` propagate to the caller.

range-scan-excludes-tombstones.text: `range_scan` filters out entries whose value equals the `TOMBSTONE` sentinel, so deleted keys are excluded from the returned pairs.

range-scan-follows-sibling-chain.text: `range_scan` walks the leaf-level linked list via `next_sibling` pointers rather than re-descending the tree, giving O(height + leaf pages in range) page reads.

range-scan-half-open-interval.text: `BTree.range_scan(start_key, end_key)` returns keys in the half-open interval `[start_key, end_key)` — start-inclusive, end-exclusive; `end_key=None` scans to the last key.

range-scan-lacks-safety-guarantees.text: Range scans are vulnerable to three independent failure modes: concurrent modifications produce inconsistent results (no snapshot isolation), corrupted sibling pointers can cause infinite traversal (no cycle guard), and large result sets consume unbounded memory (eager materialization into a list).

justifications.label: Three distinct safety gaps each independently threaten range scan correctness or availability

range-scan-last-writer-wins.text: `range_scan` iterates sources oldest-to-newest (SSTables, then immutable memtables, then active memtable) so that dict overwrites naturally give each key the value from the newest source

range-scan-materializes-results.text: `range_scan` collects all matching `(key, value)` pairs into a list in memory rather than yielding lazily; large ranges consume proportional memory.

range-scan-merges-memtable-and-sstables.text: `range_scan()` combines results from both the active memtable and all SSTables in `self._sstables`, making it sensitive to mutations of either data structure during iteration

range-scan-newer-wins-by-priority.text: The range scan merge uses an incrementing priority counter where higher priority = newer source; the dict naturally deduplicates by overwriting older entries for the same key

range-scan-no-bound-order-validation.text: `range_scan` does not validate that `end_key >= start_key`; passing `end_key < start_key` returns an empty list instead of raising an error.

range-scan-no-concurrency-protection.text: `range_scan` can observe inconsistent state if a flush or compaction runs concurrently, since there is no snapshot isolation or locking

range-scan-no-cycle-guard.text: `range_scan` has no visited-set or cycle detection on the leaf sibling chain; a corrupted `next_sibling` pointer would cause an infinite loop.

range-scan-no-mutation.text: `Partition.range_scan` is a pure read operation with no side effects — it never modifies `_keys`, `_values`, or any other state, and returns a fresh list the caller can mutate freely.

range-scan-non-string-bounds-cause-typee.text: `Partition.range_scan` does not validate bound types; passing a non-string `start` or `end` causes a `TypeError` from comparisons inside `bisect_left`.

range-scan-none-end-scans-unbounded.text: Passing `end=None` to `Partition.range_scan` sets the right boundary to `len(self._keys)`, scanning from `start` through the last key with no upper bound.

range-scan-priority-field-unused.text: The priority integer stored in the `merged` dict during `range_scan` is never read or compared; correctness relies entirely on the source iteration order and dict overwrite semantics, making the priority field dead weight

range-scan-pure-read.text: `range_scan` has no side effects: it does not mutate tree state, trigger flushes, or modify the WAL

range-scan-relies-on-sorted-keys.text: `range_scan` correctness depends on `_keys` being sorted, an invariant maintained by `put`/`delete`/`split`/`merge` but not enforced structurally — direct mutation of `_keys` bypassing these methods silently produces wrong results.

range-scan-returns-sorted-pairs.text: `range_scan` returns a `List[Tuple[str, str]]` of `(key, value)` pairs sorted in lexicographic key order.

range-scan-reversed-range-returns-empty.text: If `start >= end`, `Partition.range_scan` returns an empty list rather than raising an error.

range-scan-snapshots-memtable-before-sst.text: range_scan() first snapshots the memtable, then iterates SSTables.

range-scan-start-beyond-max-returns-empt.text: If `start_key` is greater than every key in the B-tree, `range_scan` returns an empty list.

range-scan-supports-unbounded.text: Calling `range_scan(start_key)` without an `end_key` scans from `start_key` through the last key in the rightmost leaf, terminating at the `NO_SIBLING` sentinel

range-scan-touches-first-and-last-partit.text: `RangePartitionedStore.range_scan` identifies the first and last relevant partitions and concatenates their results.

range-scan-uses-bisect-left-for-both-bou.text: `Partition.range_scan` uses `bisect.bisect_left` for both the inclusive lower bound and the exclusive upper bound of the half-open interval.

range-scan-zip-silently-truncates-mismat.text: If `_keys` and `_values` diverge in length, `Partition.range_scan`'s `zip` silently truncates results to the shorter list.

reaches-called-exclusively-by-happens-be.text: `_reaches` is a private helper called exclusively by `happens_before`.

reaches-does-not-mutate-event-graph.text: `_reaches` is a pure function that reads the event graph but never mutates it.

reaches-performs-backward-bfs-from-targe.text: `_reaches` performs a backward BFS from `target` through `_parent` and `_cause` edges to check whether `source` is reachable.

reaches-returns-true-when-source-is-targ.text: If `source is target`, `_reaches` returns `True` on the first iteration due to the identity check.

reaches-uses-identity-not-equality.text: `_reaches` uses `is` (object identity) to find the source event, not `==`, because dataclass equality would conflate distinct events with identical field values.

reaches-walks-two-edge-types.text: The causal graph has two edge types: `_parent` (same-node sequential) and `_cause` (cross-node send→receive), and `_reaches` must follow both to correctly determine happens-before.

read-all-records-is-lazy-generator.text: `_read_all_records` returns a lazy `Iterator[WALRecord]` generator rather than materializing all records.

read-all-records-no-internal-lock.text: `_read_all_records` does not acquire `self._lock`; thread safety during iteration is the caller's responsibility.

read-all-records-propagates-os-errors.text: `_read_all_records` does not catch filesystem `OSError` from opening or reading files; such errors propagate to the caller.

read-all-records-requires-caller-flush.text: `_read_all_records` does not flush the write file descriptor; both `replay` and `iterate` must call `self._fd.flush()` before iterating.

read-all-records-yields-all-operation-ty.text: `_read_all_records` yields all WAL record types (PUT, DELETE, COMMIT, CHECKPOINT); filtering is the caller's responsibility.

read-all-records-yields-in-write-order.text: `_read_all_records` yields records in file order from `_wal_files()` and then byte-offset order within each file, matching write order.

read-path-anticipates-concurrent-flush.text: Both `get()` (line 254) and `range_scan()` (line 286) check `_immutable_memtables` in the correct order, indicating the read path was designed for a concurrent-flush architecture that the write path never implements

read-path-unreliable-from-storage-throug.text: The complete read path from storage through derived systems is unreliable at every stage: the SSTable layer has compounding integrity and performance deficiencies (no per-entry checksums, linear miss-probes from missing Bloom integration, redundant key-list rebuilds per lookup) while the CDC backbone feeding all derived systems depends on reconstruction heuristics for event semantics and requires callers to manually flush and provide old values for consistency.

justifications.label: Storage-layer integrity deficiencies feed directly into the CDC pipeline that derived systems depend on, making the entire storage-to-projection data path untrustworthy.

read-predicate-adds-matched-keys-to-read.text: read_predicate adds every key that matches the predicate to tx._read_set, so standard read-write conflict detection also covers predicate-read keys.

read-predicate-deps-only-for-committed.text: `read_predicate` records dependency graph edges only for keys in the committed snapshot (`k in snap`), not for keys the transaction itself created via `write()` — avoiding self-dependencies

read-predicate-stores-result-snapshot.text: `read_predicate` appends a `(predicate, dict(result))` tuple to `tx._predicate_locks` — a deep copy so `commit()` can compare against the original result even after database state changes

read-predicate-uses-start-timestamp.text: read_predicate calls _snapshot(tx.start_timestamp) to build the base view before merging the transaction's own buffered writes and removing its pending deletes.

read-repair-get-selects-highest-version.text: ReadRepairStore.get reads the first R available replicas and selects the response with the highest version as the winning value.

read-repair-only-fixes-queried-replicas.text: Duplicates `read-repair-scope-is-quorum-only` — already captured that `ReadRepairStore.get()` only repairs the R replicas selected for the quorum read.

read-repair-put-writes-first-w-available.text: ReadRepairStore.put writes the newly computed version to the first W available replicas in replica order.

read-repair-raises-insufficient-replicas.text: ReadRepairStore raises InsufficientReplicasError when fewer replicas are available than the read or write quorum requires.

read-repair-replica-selection-determinis.text: ReadRepairStore selects replicas deterministically as the first N available replicas, with no randomization or load balancing.

read-repair-resurrects-deleted-keys.text: `DynamoCluster.get()` read repair pushes the highest-versioned value to stale replicas, so a naive delete (removing from `_store`) is undone when a recovering node still holds the old value

read-repair-scope-is-quorum-only.text: Read repair in `get()` only fixes replicas that were part of the read quorum, not all replicas; full-cluster repair requires a separate call to `anti_entropy_repair()`.
