stream-join-has-no-right-join-type.text: The `JoinType` enum contains only `INNER`, `LEFT`, and `FULL_OUTER`; there is no `RIGHT`, so right-join semantics require swapping the configured stream names.

stream-join-inner-requires-key-and-windo.text: Inner join only produces a `JoinResult` when both key equality and `|t_left - t_right| <= window_duration` hold; either condition failing alone prevents a match.

stream-join-late-events-dropped-silently.text: Events arriving after `watermark - allowed_lateness` are dropped and counted in `stats.late_events_dropped`; the processor never raises exceptions for late arrivals.

stream-join-late-events-silently-dropped.text: Events with timestamp below `watermark - allowed_lateness` are silently dropped, with only the `late_events_dropped` counter incremented.

stream-join-left-asymmetric.text: `JoinType.LEFT` emits misses only for unmatched left-side events; unmatched right-side events are silently dropped without any miss emission

stream-join-left-miss-emitted-on-expirat.text: Duplicates `stream-join-miss-deferred` — unmatched events emit misses only when `advance_time` expires them, not eagerly.

stream-join-matched-left-event-not-misse.text: In a LEFT join, a left event that matched a right event does not also produce a miss result when it is later expired.

stream-join-miss-deferred.text: Outer-join misses are only emitted at event expiration time (when timestamp falls below watermark minus window duration), never eagerly on arrival

stream-join-no-stream-validation.text: The processor does not validate that an event's `stream_name` matches either configured stream; an unknown stream name is silently treated as the right stream via `_is_left` returning `False`

stream-join-one-to-many.text: A single event can match multiple events on the opposite side; the matched flag is set on all participants, so none produce outer-join misses

stream-join-probes-on-arrival.text: `StreamJoinProcessor` buffers an arriving event and immediately probes it against the opposite buffer.

stream-join-process-event-returns-immedi.text: `process_event()` returns matches synchronously on each call (push-based) rather than batching to a flush boundary; results are available the instant a match is found.

stream-join-process-event-returns-new-re.text: `process_event` returns only the results produced during that call while still accumulating all results in the shared `_results` list.

stream-join-result-timestamp-later-of-tw.text: `JoinResult.join_timestamp` is set to the later of the two matched events' timestamps.

stream-join-watermark-monotonic.text: The join processor's watermark only advances forward via `max(current, event.timestamp)`; `advance_time()` silently ignores timestamps at or below the current watermark

stream-version-derived-from-list-length.text: stream_version derives a stream's version from the length of its event list rather than from a separately stored version counter.

stream-version-is-event-count.text: `stream_version()` returns the count of events in a stream (not the latest `event_id`), and `expected_version` checks against this count for optimistic concurrency

structural-mutations-eventually-write-me.text: Every B-tree structural mutation (insert, delete, split, page allocation, page free) eventually calls `_write_meta` to persist the updated tree shape.

subscriber-dispatch-is-synchronous.text: Event subscriber notification in `EventStore` blocks the `append()` caller — projections update on the writer's thread before the append call returns, trading throughput for zero-gap consistency

subtle-corruption-deferred-detection.text: Covered by existing beliefs `hint-corrupt-worse-than-missing` (silent bad offsets) and `bitcask-crc32-raises-corruption-error` (CRC mismatch at read time)

superversion-refcount-defers-sstable-del.text: In the `SuperVersion` pattern, old SSTable files are deleted only when the last reader using that version releases its reference.

superversion-refcount-delays-old-sstable.text: A RocksDB iterator increments its SuperVersion's reference count, and compaction can install a new SuperVersion while the old SuperVersion and its SSTables stay alive until the last iterator releases the reference.

sync-all-two-rounds-suffices.text: `CRDTReplicaGroup.sync_all` runs exactly 2 rounds of all-pairs sync, which is sufficient for convergence of any state-based CRDT with a commutative/associative/idempotent merge

sync-mode-hdd-throughput-cap.text: In `"sync"` mode, performing one `fsync` per write caps throughput at roughly 100–200 writes/sec on HDD because an `fsync` takes 5–10ms.

sync-mode-none-relies-on-os-dirty-expiry.text: In the WAL's implicit `"none"` sync mode, durability relies on the OS flushing dirty page-cache pages, typically within 30 seconds on Linux as controlled by `vm.dirty_expire_centisecs`, with no guarantee.

sync-mode-none-skips-per-write-fsync.text: When `sync_mode="none"`, the per-write `_do_sync()` call (default `force=False`) is a complete no-op — no fsync and no batch queue — trading durability for maximum write throughput

sync-return-counts-apply-remote-change-c.text: `MultiLeaderCluster.sync()` returns the number of `apply_remote_change` calls, including idempotent skips, rather than the number of accepted changes.

system-converges-on-permanent-dark-failu.text: The system converges on permanent dark failure: there is no operational path to correctness at any scale AND failure is irreversible and undetectable, meaning the system silently accumulates data loss with no diagnostic signal, operational remedy, or evolutionary escape — even the decision to rebuild requires evidence the system cannot produce.

justifications.label: Combining the absence of any path to correctness with the invisibility of failure yields the emergent property that the system degrades without anyone knowing it is degrading.

system-degrades-monotonically-at-every-a.text: The system degrades monotonically at every abstraction level with no equilibrium: storage engines erode structurally with no self-healing (leaked pages, growing height, no rebalancing, unsafe recovery), and the distributed layer's compensating mechanisms (anti-entropy, read repair) cannot fully resolve the resulting replica divergence, which accumulates without bound.

justifications.label: Storage degradation feeds unresolvable distributed divergence — neither layer has mechanisms to reverse entropy

system-failure-is-undetectable-and-irrev.text: The system's natural trajectory is toward permanent undetectable data loss: corruption propagates silently through every pipeline without detection, AND the structural degradation that enables it is irreversible at every abstraction level — failure is invisible while it happens and unfixable after it's discovered.

justifications.label: Silent loss (no detection at any pipeline stage) combined with irreversible degradation (no self-healing at any layer) means failures compound monotonically without any observable signal or recovery path

system-has-no-stable-operational-regime.text: The system has no stable operational regime at any scale: storage degrades monotonically during normal operation with no self-healing, failures widen correctness gaps at every abstraction level, and no storage paradigm can escape by scaling (hash indexes hit memory walls, LSM hits probe walls) — the architecture converges toward failure under every operating condition.

justifications.label: Three independent degradation vectors (structural erosion, failure amplification, scalability walls) leave no stable equilibrium

system-has-no-undo-at-any-layer.text: No layer in the system can reverse a completed operation: the WAL stores only new values with no before-images (making rollback structurally impossible), and transaction abort is a status-flag change that leaves all written versions on disk, meaning neither the storage layer nor the logical transaction layer supports undo.

justifications.label: WAL redo-only format and MVCC status-only abort independently confirm no undo capability exists at any layer

system-neither-verifiable-nor-repairable.text: The system is trapped in a verification-repair deadlock: verification is impossible at every architectural layer (integrity checks degrade along the pipeline, protocol safety is unfalsifiable under current testing) AND the rigid binary format design across the storage stack prevents adding verification or self-healing capabilities through evolution, foreclosing both detection and correction of faults.

justifications.label: Independent impossibility of verification and repair closes both halves of the detect-and-fix loop — you cannot find the problems and you cannot change the formats to make them findable.

term-partitioned-async-is-eventually-con.text: Substantially overlaps with existing belief `async-index-defers-mutations`, which already captures that mutations are queued and `flush_index()` must be called.

term-partitioned-point-query-is-targeted.text: `TermPartitionedDB.query_by_field` looks up a single index partition by term hash then fetches documents from their home partitions, touching 1 + K partitions (K = distinct data partitions) instead of scattering to all.

term-partitioned-query-hits-one-partitio.text: `TermPartitionedDB` routes an index-term query to exactly one partition.

term-partitioned-range-query-scans-all.text: TermPartitionedDB.query_range scans all partitions for range matches, so it does not retain the targeted-query advantage of term-partitioned point lookups.

term-partitioned-supports-range-query.text: TermPartitionedDB supports query_range() for range-partitioned terms, as exercised by TestRangeQuery with query_range("color", "a", "d").

term-partitioned-write-touches-multiple.text: `TermPartitionedDB.put` touches 1 + N partitions where N depends on how many distinct index partitions the document's field values hash to, because index entries live on term-hashed partitions separate from the data partition.

test-block-size-differs-from-default.text: Tests universally use `block_size=4` while `SSTableWriter` defaults to 64 and `lsm.py` defaults to 16; the small test value forces multi-block index paths with small datasets

test-equivocating-byzantine-preserves-co.text: The `test_equivocating_byzantine` test confirms equivocating digest messages do not disrupt consensus.

test-event-store-only-tests-concurrency-.text: The only explicit error path tested by `test_event_store.py` is optimistic concurrency via `pytest.raises(ConcurrencyConflict)`; it does not test invalid event types, missing fields, or corrupt persistence.

test-event-store-seed-account-produces-b.text: `_seed_account` appends four events to `account:1` (open balance 0, deposit 100, withdraw 30, deposit 50) and produces a final balance of 120.

test-lamport-five-node-chain-tests-trans.text: `test_five_node_chain` uses a 5-node linear message chain (N0→N1→N2→N3→N4) to verify total order consistency and transitive happens-before across the full chain.

test-lamport-has-no-fixtures-or-setup.text: Every test in `test_lamport.py` constructs its own `Node` instances from scratch with no fixtures or setup.

test-lamport-imports-only-local-lamport-.text: `test_lamport.py` imports all entities from `lamport.py` in the same directory and uses no external libraries, including pytest.

test-lamport-inline-runner-iterates-glob.text: The `if __name__ == "__main__"` block iterates over `globals()` to find and run all `test_*` functions.

test-lamport-no-error-handling.text: Tests rely on `assert` statements; failures raise `AssertionError`, and the inline runner does not catch exceptions.

test-lamport-self-comparison-returns-non.text: `happens_before(e, e, [e])` returns `None`, enforcing irreflexivity of the strict partial order.

test-sync-modes-does-not-verify-durabili.text: The `test_sync_modes` test in `test_wal.py` only checks that the WAL does not crash for each sync mode; it does not verify durability semantics.

test-verify-reconstruct-up-to-two-balanc.text: In `test_verify.py`, `reconstruct_state` with `up_to=2` replays only AccountOpened and MoneyDeposited, yielding balance 100.

test-wal-basic-lacks-crash-mid-batch-tes.text: test_basic in test_wal.py verifies that replay() returns the correct count of PUT/DELETE records but includes no test for crash-mid-batch recovery.

test-wal-corruption-verifies-only-first-.text: test_corruption in test_wal.py corrupts the last 5 bytes of a WAL file and verifies that only the uncorrupted first record survives replay.

test-wrong-digest-byzantine-preserves-co.text: The `test_wrong_digest_byzantine` test confirms honest nodes still reach agreement when one node sends bad digests.

tester-and-original-tests-coexist.text: Implied by existing beliefs `pytest-files-have-broader-coverage`, `both-suites-discoverable-by-pytest`, and `tester-files-are-standalone-runnable`; no new invariant added

tester-bitcask-auto-compaction-bounds-se.text: `test_auto_compaction` uses `auto_compact_threshold=3` and `max_segment_size=50` and asserts `num_segments <= 5` after 50 writes.

tester-bitcask-crc-corruption-flips-payl.text: `test_crc_corruption` flips a byte at `offset + HEADER_SIZE + 2`, inside the payload, and asserts `get` raises `CorruptionError`.

tester-bitcask-fault-injection-mutates-r.text: The tester file's CRC-corruption and partial-write tests directly mutate segment file bytes using `struct.pack` and raw file I/O rather than mocking.

tester-bitcask-fixture-forces-rotation.text: The `store` fixture constructs `BitcaskStore` with `max_segment_size=100` and `auto_compact_threshold=100`, so segment rotation occurs after only a few writes.

tester-bitcask-large-dataset-10k.text: `test_large_dataset` inserts 10,000 keys with 5,000 overwrites and spot-checks both updated and untouched keys.

tester-bitcask-suite-covers-eight-proper.text: The tester file validates eight behavioral properties: basic CRUD, segment rotation, compaction, CRC integrity, hint-file recovery, partial-write tolerance, auto-compaction, and large-dataset correctness.

tester-bitcask-tempdir-isolation.text: Each tester Bitcask test uses `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory` to create an isolated store directory that is cleaned up by the context manager.

tester-covers-full-dynamo-lifecycle-inte.text: `leaderless-replication/test_dynamo_tester.py:test_spec_example_full` exercises the entire Dynamo lifecycle including write, read, node failure, degraded quorum write, recovery, read repair, quorum failure, and anti-entropy in a single test.

tester-dev-suites-overlap-not-hierarchic.text: The tester and developer test suites have overlapping but non-hierarchical coverage: tester files uniquely test spec-example compliance and cross-path equivalence, while dev files uniquely test crash recovery and internal state

tester-label-denotes-qa-validation-role.text: Filenames such as `leaderless-replication/test_dynamo_tester.py` and `unbundled-database/test_tester_validation.py` use docstrings that explicitly label them as QA/tester-stage validation artifacts.

tester-main-block-appears-in-13-modules.text: The `if __name__ == '__main__':` block pattern appears in `tester_test_*.py` files across 13 modules.

tester-naming-avoids-pytest-discovery.text: The `tester_test_*.py` prefix does not match pytest's default collection patterns (`test_*.py` / `*_test.py`), so these files are excluded from `pytest` runs unless explicitly specified

tester-output-is-human-readable.text: Duplicates existing belief `tester-files-use-stdout-validation` which already captures the stdout PASSED/FAILED reporting convention

tester-test-dual-runner.text: Some `tester_test_*.py` files are pytest-only (using fixtures/`pytest.raises`), while others include an `if __name__ == '__main__':` block for standalone execution; the two execution patterns coexist across modules

tester-test-files-are-runnable-test-suit.text: Each `tester_test_*.py` file contains runnable `def test_*` functions that assert behavior, not harness or infrastructure code.

tester-test-no-shared-harness.text: There is no shared `conftest.py`, base class, or test harness across `tester_test_*.py` files; each imports only its own module under test plus standard library utilities and is fully self-contained

tester-test-wal-has-ten-test-functions.text: `write-ahead-log/tester_test_wal.py` contains 10 test functions covering appends, crash recovery, corruption, truncation, rotation, iteration, empty WAL, large values, checkpoint replay, and sequence monotonicity across restart.

tester-test-wal-prints-pass-per-test.text: `tester_test_wal.py` prints a pass message from each test function and prints `ALL TESTS PASSED` at the end of its `__main__` block.

tester-tests-are-distilled-specs.text: Each `tester_test_*.py` is a simplified subset of its corresponding `test_*.py`, organized by numbered behavioral properties (`# 1. No false negatives`, `# 2. FPR within 2x of target`) rather than exhaustive edge cases

tester-tests-are-zero-dependency.text: Duplicates existing belief `tester-files-are-standalone-runnable` which already captures that these files run independently of any test framework

tester-tests-have-spec-aligned-docstring.text: `tester_test_*.py` test functions include docstrings that mirror spec requirements (e.g., `test_determinism` has the docstring `"Same key always maps to same node."`), unlike `test_*.py` functions which generally lack such docstrings.

tester-tests-not-auto-regenerated.text: `tester_test_*.py` files contain no auto-generation markers (`generated`, `DO NOT EDIT`) and no regeneration tooling exists in the documented code-expert workflow; they are static committed files

tester-tests-print-passed-markers.text: Tester test files end each test with `print('test_xxx PASSED')`, making silence a secondary failure signal in addition to pytest's exit code.

tester-tests-public-contract.text: `tester_test_*.py` files test the public API contract of each implementation, importing only public symbols (plus format constants for fault injection), acting as external conformance harnesses

tester-versions-have-more-test-functions.text: The `tester_test_*.py` files consistently contain more test functions than their `test_*.py` counterparts (bloom-filter: 11 vs 5, gossip-protocol: 12 vs 10), and include tests for features not covered in the default-discovered files

testing-covers-neither-crash-nor-async-f.text: The testing methodology covers neither single-node crash failures nor distributed asynchronous failures: crash recovery paths are systematically untested (no torn-write tests, no compaction crash tests), and distributed protocols are validated only under synchronous deterministic simulation with no real network I/O — the entire failure surface area from storage crashes to network partitions is invisible to the test suite.

justifications.label: Two conclusions at different depths both identify testing blind spots — one for storage-layer crashes (depth-1), one for protocol-layer async behavior (depth-2) — spanning the full stack

textbook-btree-merge-propagates-underflo.text: In textbook B-tree deletion, a merge that causes underflow can propagate upward and potentially shrink the root.

textbook-btree-minimum-fill-invariant.text: Textbook B-tree deletion maintains a minimum fill invariant where every non-root node has at least ceil(m/2) keys for order m.

time-window-contains-uses-absolute-diffe.text: `TimeWindow.contains(t1, t2)` checks whether the absolute difference between two timestamps is within the configured duration, making the match symmetric in arrival order.

tob-competing-proposals-bump-rounds.text: When a TOB slot is decided by another proposer with a different value, the losing node re-proposes its value for a new slot rather than retrying the same slot with a higher round

tob-consensus-uses-paxos-ballot-numbers.text: `ConsensusInstance.prepare(n)` / `accept(n, val)` use monotonic proposal numbers where a higher prepare preempts a lower one, causing `accept` with a stale number to return `{accepted: False}`

tob-contiguous-delivery.text: Messages are delivered to the application only when all prior slots are decided; `_next_slot` advances through a contiguous run, and a gap (undecided slot N when N+1 is decided) blocks all later delivery

tob-full-paxos-per-slot.text: Every slot in Total Order Broadcast runs the complete two-phase Paxos protocol (Prepare→Promise→Accept→Accepted) from scratch; no state carries between slots to skip Phase 1

tob-linearizable-reads-via-broadcast.text: `LinearizableRegister.read()` broadcasts the read through consensus rather than reading locally, establishing a consistent point in the total order — necessary for linearizability without leader leases

tob-linearizable-register-is-built-on-br.text: `LinearizableRegister` wraps `TOBCluster` to provide `write()`/`read()`/`compare_and_set()`, demonstrating the DDIA Chapter 9 equivalence between total-order broadcast and linearizable storage

tob-no-leader-concept.text: TOBNode has no leader election or lease mechanism; any node can propose for any undecided slot at any time, making it vulnerable to competing proposals

tob-no-persistent-storage.text: TOBNode crash/recovery uses state transfer from peers via `force_decide()` on each missed slot; there is no WAL, persistent log, or on-disk state — all durability depends on a majority staying alive

tob-ordering-verified-under-real-failure.text: Total Order Broadcast maintains identical delivery ordering across node failures: recovered nodes deliver the same slot sequence as live nodes, confirming that per-slot Paxos consensus and contiguous slot delivery enforce a single global order even through failure and recovery.

justifications.label: Ordering correctness across failures is proven only under synchronous simulation, not asynchronous networks

tob-paxos-per-slot.text: Each slot in the total order log is decided by an independent single-decree Paxos instance (`ConsensusInstance`); there is no stable-leader optimization or Multi-Paxos Phase 1 skip

tob-preempted-value-requeued.text: When a proposer's value loses its slot to a competing value, the original is pushed back onto `_pending` for proposal in a later slot, ensuring no broadcast messages are silently dropped

tob-proposal-number-encoded-round-n-plus.text: `_make_proposal_number(round_num)` generates globally unique proposal numbers as `round * N + node_id`.

tob-proposal-number-encodes-node-id.text: Proposal numbers are computed as `round * num_nodes + node_id`, guaranteeing uniqueness across nodes within the same round but restarting at round 0 for each slot independently

tob-quorum-is-strict-majority.text: The TOB cluster uses 3 nodes where 2 can make progress but 1 alone cannot, confirming a strict-majority quorum requirement for both Paxos Phase 1 and Phase 2

tob-recovery-replays-missed-slots.text: After `recover_node()`, the recovered node's delivery order matches live nodes' order, meaning recovery replays all consensus decisions made while the node was down via state transfer

tob-route-messages-recursion-depth-limit.text: `TOBCluster._route_messages` has a recursion depth limit of 500 to prevent stack overflow during contention.

tob-start-proposal-sends-prepare-to-all-.text: `_start_proposal` sends `prepare` messages to every node, including the proposing node itself.

tob-test-suite-contains-14-tests.text: `test_total_order_broadcast.py` contains 14 test functions covering delivery, fault tolerance, consensus internals, linearizable register operations, and ordering invariants.

tob-test-uses-closure-factory-for-callba.text: Test 14 uses a `make_cb(node_id)` closure factory so each delivery callback captures a distinct node ID.

tob-tests-create-fresh-3-node-cluster.text: Each TOB test constructs a fresh `TOBCluster(3)` with no shared fixtures or setup.

tob-uses-single-decree-paxos-per-slot.text: Each slot in the total order broadcast is decided by an independent `ConsensusInstance` running single-decree Paxos with prepare/accept phases (`total_order_broadcast.py:3`).

tob-value-adoption-on-prepare.text: In `_handle_prepare_response`, if any acceptor reports a previously accepted value, the proposer must adopt the one with the highest proposal number — this is the core Paxos safety invariant preventing decided values from being overwritten

tob-vulnerable-to-dueling-proposer-livel.text: The per-slot Paxos design is vulnerable to livelock when two nodes propose for the same slot simultaneously.

tombstone-encoded-in-value-not-header.text: Neither `hash-index-storage/bitcask.py` nor `log-structured-hash-table/bitcask.py` uses a header flag for tombstones; deletion status is encoded in the value payload instead (empty string vs. magic byte sentinel).

tombstone-lifecycle-fragmented-across-mo.text: Tombstone management is handled differently at every layer: the LSM uses an ambiguous empty-bytes sentinel indistinguishable from empty values, compaction preserves tombstones by default with caller-controlled removal, and distributed deletion requires cross-replica convergence before safe removal — with no coordination between these concerns.

justifications.label: Three layers of the tombstone lifecycle (creation, local cleanup, distributed cleanup) are independently implemented with no shared abstraction or safety contract

tombstone-lifetime-space-safety-tradeoff.text: General distributed systems design principle (longer tombstone lifetimes waste space but tolerate longer outages) rather than a testable claim about this codebase's behavior.

tombstone-marker-single-byte-no-redundan.text: The tombstone/value distinction in `sstable-and-compaction/sstable.py` rests on a single byte (`0xFF` vs first byte of a 4-byte value length), making it vulnerable to single-bit corruption that silently converts live entries to deletions or vice versa

tombstone-removal-requires-full-key-cove.text: A tombstone for key K can only be safely removed during compaction if every SSTable that could contain an older entry for K is included in that compaction run; otherwise the deleted key can be resurrected from a surviving SSTable

tombstone-removes-cross-segment.text: A tombstone record in segment N removes the key from `_index` even if the key's live value was written in an earlier segment, because the index is a flat dict shared across all segment scans.

tombstone-reported-as-none-in-conflict.text: `ConflictRecord.remote_value` reports `None` for tombstoned changes rather than the internal `_TOMBSTONE` sentinel; callers see deletion as `None` and never observe the sentinel object.

tombstone-sentinel-is-a-forbidden-value.text: Storing `b"__BITCASK_TOMBSTONE__"` as a legitimate value in `log-structured-hash-table` causes silent data loss on next recovery, as `_scan_segment` interprets it as a delete — the sentinel is an implicit API constraint with no validation

topics-json-references-tester-generation.text: `.code-expert/topics.json` line 1987 contains a topic asking how the code-expert workflow generates `tester_test_*.py` files from specs.

topn-output-is-descending.text: `TopN` returns results ordered descending by the specified field (for top 5, `top5[0][1] >= top5[4][1]`).

topn-uses-bounded-heap.text: `TopN` uses an O(N) bounded heap and yields only at the end, making it a partial materialization stage.

topology-creates-divergence-window-not-c.text: Replication topology affects only the duration of observable divergence, not the final convergence outcome: all topologies use identical deterministic LWW resolution, but ring topology creates O(N) rounds of divergence while all-to-all converges in O(1) — with no adaptive topology switching, the system cannot minimize the divergence window in response to cluster size or partition conditions.

justifications.label: Same eventual outcome but O(N) vs O(1) observable divergence window with static topology selection

topology-does-not-change-conflict-outcom.text: Both topologies use the same deterministic `(timestamp, node_id)` comparison for LWW resolution; topology affects when and where conflicts are detected, not which value wins.

torn-length-prefix-causes-silent-skip.text: If a torn write corrupts the 4-byte length prefix in `wal.py:_read_record`, the reader interprets garbage as `record_length`, reads that many bytes (consuming valid subsequent records as data), then returns `None` on short read — no error is raised and no resync is attempted

torn-write-after-valid-prefix-detected-b.text: If a crash interrupts a multi-sector write after the record length prefix and early fields are committed, _read_record sees a complete record but a CRC mismatch catches the stale tail.

transaction-isolation-composes-two-invar.text: Serializable snapshot isolation is achieved by composing two complementary invariant layers: MVCC provides visibility correctness (append-only versions, own-writes guarantee, symmetric deletion visibility) while SSI adds serializability enforcement (read-only optimization, committed-only snapshots, write-delete mutual exclusion).

justifications.label: MVCC handles what a transaction can see while SSI handles what it can do — neither is sufficient alone

transaction-isolation-fragile-under-rest.text: Transaction isolation's carefully composed two-invariant-layer model (MVCC visibility plus SSI conflict detection) is fragile under restart: abort is a status-change-only operation that leaves written data on disk, and MVCC counters that must be monotonic have no persistence mechanism, so a crash both resurrects aborted writes and breaks the ordering invariant that determines visibility.

justifications.label: The composed isolation model depends on volatile state that crashes destroy

transaction-recovery-has-no-crash-path.text: Transaction abort is a status-change-only operation with no disk rollback, and MVCC correctness depends on monotonic counters that have no persistence mechanism, meaning a crash simultaneously leaves aborted-transaction writes on disk and resets the ordering counters that determine visibility — both invariants fail together.

justifications.label: Both abort cleanup and ordering invariants exist only in volatile memory

transfer-dict-keyed-by-arc.text: The transfer dict uses `(arc_start, arc_end)` tuples as keys, so two vnodes producing identical arc boundaries would silently overwrite rather than accumulate.

transfer-test-weak-assertions.text: `test_add_node_returns_transfers` only asserts transfer direction (A→B) and existence, not arc non-overlap or total size correctness — the code is correct but the test doesn't prove it.

tree-height-monotonically-increases.text: Since neither the reference implementation nor PostgreSQL merges internal nodes on delete, tree height only grows (on root splits) and never shrinks, even under heavy deletion

truncate-advances-base-offset-additively.text: `Topic.truncate` updates `_base_offsets[partition]` with `+= actual`, a relative shift, because it only removes a contiguous prefix from the front of the partition log.

truncate-caps-count-to-log-length.text: Topic.truncate computes actual = min(count, len(log)) before slicing the partition log.

truncate-plus-per-record-crc-is-dangerou.text: The non-atomic `truncate()` in `wal.py` can produce reordered or incomplete files that pass per-record CRC validation; chained checksums would detect the corruption at the chain break point

truncated-page-breaks-deserialization.text: If PageManager.write_page truncates a page, _deserialize_leaf will try to unpack the header's declared key count from missing bytes, causing a struct.unpack error or corrupted data.

truncation-preserves-contiguous-offsets-.text: Truncation removes only a contiguous prefix, so surviving offsets remain contiguous unless compaction previously created gaps.

tumbling-aggregator-closes-window-at-end.text: `TumblingWindowAggregator.advance_time(t)` closes every window whose end (`window_start + duration`) is less than or equal to the current window start derived from `t`.

tumbling-window-aligned-to-zero.text: `TumblingWindowAggregator` aligns window boundaries to multiples of the window size starting from 0 — windows are `[0, size)`, `[size, 2*size)`, etc., not relative to the first event's timestamp.

tumbling-window-floor-division.text: `TumblingWindowAggregator` assigns windows by floor-dividing the timestamp by window size, producing aligned non-overlapping boundaries regardless of when events arrive

def _window_key(self, timestamp):
    return int(timestamp // self._window.duration)

two-incompatible-conflict-resolution-par.text: The codebase contains two mathematically incompatible conflict resolution paradigms with no bridge between them: CRDTs provide algebraically proven convergence (idempotent, commutative merge satisfying SEC requirements), while the multi-leader strategy pattern offers LWW and custom-merge without formal convergence guarantees, and no mechanism exists to compose or translate between them.

justifications.label: CRDT merge algebra and strategy-pattern resolution solve the same problem with incompatible formalisms

two-rename-sites-in-compaction.text: Covered by `rename-without-dir-barrier`; the specific count/location of rename call sites is unstable detail.

two-sstable-implementations-same-pattern.text: `lsm.py` (using `sparse_index_interval=16` and `bisect`) and `sstable.py` (using `block_size=64` and manual binary search) implement the same sparse-index-with-block-scan pattern with different defaults, naming, and file format maturity

two-tombstone-strategies-diverge.text: Covered by existing beliefs `bitcask-tombstone-is-empty-string` (hash-index uses `value_size == 0`) and `log-structured-sentinel-is-in-band` (log-structured uses sentinel byte string)

two-wal-designs-in-repo.text: The standalone `wal.py` uses a logical WAL (keyed PUT/DELETE operations with COMMIT markers) while `btree.py` uses a physical WAL (raw page images); they solve different problems and have different recovery semantics

unbound-schedulers-cause-cache-migration.text: General systems knowledge about OS thread scheduling, not a codebase-specific claim.

unbundled-catch-up-false-starts-empty.text: A derived system added with catch_up=False starts empty and processes only future writes, not existing data.

unbundled-catchup-directly-sets-private-.text: CDCStream.snapshot_and_stream() directly assigns to the consumer's _position attribute to position a late-joining derived system.

unbundled-catchup-produces-consistent-de.text: Catch-up via snapshot and streaming produces consistent derived-system state equivalent to full event replay, because WAL entries are ordered by LSN and the rebuild protocol is verified to match full replay output.

justifications.label: Catch-up correctness depends on position tracking that exists only in volatile memory

unbundled-catchup-rebuild-equivalence.text: Catch-up via `snapshot_and_stream` and rebuild via full CDC event replay must produce identical derived-system state, verified by comparing `get_state()` output from two independent derived systems

unbundled-cdc-update-carries-old-and-new.text: Duplicates existing belief `unbundled-db-cdc-events-carry-old-value`; the new_value presence is implicit in any CDC event representing a mutation

unbundled-database-add-derived-system-do.text: Adding a new derived system to the unbundled database requires only calling `db.add_derived_system(idx)` and the next `db.flush()` feeds pending CDC events to all registered consumers; no change to the write path is needed.

unbundled-db-catch-up-replays-full-log.text: Duplicates `unbundled-db-catch-up-replays-history` proposed above from the companion test file.

unbundled-db-catch-up-replays-history.text: A derived system added with `catch_up=True` receives all historical CDC events to reach current state, without requiring a separate snapshot mechanism.

unbundled-db-cdc-events-carry-old-value.text: Every update and delete CDC event includes the previous value (`old_value`), enabling derived systems to undo prior state; inserts have `old_value=None`.

unbundled-db-composes-via-log.text: The unbundled database wires independent subsystems (WAL, storage engine, CDC, derived systems) through a shared append-only log with independent consumer positions, applying Unix-style composition at the system architecture level

unbundled-db-flush-is-consistency-bounda.text: Duplicates `unbundled-db-flush-required-for-derived` proposed above from the companion test file.

unbundled-db-flush-required-for-derived.text: Derived systems (secondary indexes, materialized views, full-text search) only see mutations after `db.flush()` is called; writes go to WAL and storage immediately but CDC consumers are decoupled.

unbundled-db-is-log-first-cdc-is-state-f.text: The unbundled database writes to WAL before storage engine, while the CDC module writes to in-memory rows before appending the log — opposite ordering of the source-of-truth relationship

unbundled-db-put-returns-cdc-event.text: `UnbundledDatabase.put()` and `delete()` return `CDCEvent` objects directly, making CDC a synchronous, first-class part of the write API rather than a side-channel.

unbundled-db-rebuild-equals-live.text: `rebuild_system()` must produce state identical to incremental live processing — this is a tested invariant verified by capturing `get_state()` before and after rebuild.

unbundled-db-rebuild-is-idempotent.text: Duplicates `unbundled-db-rebuild-equals-live` proposed above from the companion test file.

unbundled-db-wal-lsn-starts-at-one.text: The unbundled database WAL assigns LSNs starting from 1 (not 0), with `latest_lsn == 0` indicating an empty log.

unbundled-db-wal-persistence-jsonl.text: The unbundled database's WAL supports optional file-backed persistence via a `.jsonl` file path, and a new `WriteAheadLog` instance recovers entries from that file on init.

unbundled-delete-nonexistent-returns-non.text: UnbundledDatabase.delete() on a nonexistent key is a silent no-op that returns None and creates no WAL entry or CDC event.

unbundled-flush-zeroes-lag.text: After `db.flush()`, `get_lag()` returns 0 for all derived systems, confirming all pending CDC events have been consumed

unbundled-fulltext-search-all-empty-retu.text: FullTextSearch.search_all([]) returns an empty list rather than raising an error.

unbundled-get-missing-key-returns-none.text: UnbundledDatabase.get() returns None for a missing key rather than raising KeyError.

unbundled-lsn-sequential.text: LSNs returned by the unbundled database's `put()`/`delete()` are 1-indexed and strictly sequential with no gaps

unbundled-materialized-view-clamps-count.text: MaterializedView clamps counts to zero with max(0, ...) to prevent negative counts.

unbundled-materialized-view-unknown-grou.text: Querying a MaterializedView for an unknown group key returns 0.

unbundled-nested-dict-values-roundtrip.text: Nested dict values written to UnbundledDatabase records survive write/read without corruption.

unbundled-rebuild-clears-state.text: `StorageEngine.rebuild(wal)` clears all existing data (including manually injected entries) before replaying WAL entries, ensuring no phantom or stale state survives a rebuild

unbundled-secondary-index-empty-query-re.text: Querying an empty SecondaryIndex returns an empty list rather than an error.

unbundled-storage-engine-tracks-current-.text: StorageEngine tracks its own current_lsn indicating how far it has applied WAL entries.

unbundled-storage-scan-filters-by-prefix.text: StorageEngine.scan(prefix) filters keys by the given prefix.

unbundled-tester-test-prefix-golden-suit.text: Files prefixed tester_test_ follow the repo convention for the specification-defining test suite.

unbundled-wal-entries-ordered-by-lsn.text: WAL entries in the unbundled database's `_entries` list are always in ascending LSN order, maintained by the sequential nature of `append()`

unbundled-wal-truncate-at-or-before-earl.text: Passing a cutoff less than or equal to earliest_lsn to truncate_before removes zero entries.

unbundled-wal-truncate-is-linear-scan.text: truncate_before rebuilds _entries via a full list comprehension, making it O(n) in the number of WAL entries.

unbundled-wal-truncate-keeps-gte.text: The unbundled database WAL cutoff is exclusive-below: entries with `lsn >= cutoff` are retained, entries with `lsn < cutoff` are discarded

unbundled-wal-truncate-memory-only.text: `WriteAheadLog.truncate_before` in the unbundled database removes entries from memory but does not modify the on-disk WAL file, so reloading from `persist_path` restores truncated entries

unbundled-wal-truncate-past-latest-empti.text: Passing a cutoff greater than latest_lsn to truncate_before removes all entries, leaving the WAL empty.

unbundled-wal-truncate-preserves-lsn.text: Truncation in the unbundled database WAL never resets `_next_lsn`, so appending after truncation continues with monotonically increasing LSNs

unbundled-wal-truncate-returns-removed-c.text: WriteAheadLog.truncate_before(lsn) returns the number of entries removed.

unbundled-wal-truncate-updates-earliest-.text: WriteAheadLog.truncate_before(lsn) updates earliest_lsn after removing older entries.

uncommitted-batch-records-discarded-on-r.text: Contradicts accepted belief `wal-replay-ignores-commit` and entry 1's analysis; entry 2 describes what a *correct* replay should do, not what the current implementation does — `replay()` filters by record type without batch-grouping logic

undo-logging-requires-dirty-pages-before.text: Undo logging forces dirty data pages to reach disk before the commit record so that a crash never leaves committed-but-unwritten data.

unfenced-resource-server-accepts-all-wri.text: The `UnfencedResourceServer.write` method accepts every write unconditionally, with no token validation.

unfenced-server-accepts-all.text: `UnfencedResourceServer` has no token parameter on `write()` and accepts all writes unconditionally, serving as the pedagogical unsafe baseline for comparison with `FencedResourceServer`

unhandled-event-types-silently-skipped.text: Events whose `event_type` has no entry in the handlers dict are skipped without warning in both `reconstruct_state` and `Projection.catch_up`

unlatched-btree-split-can-hide-sibling-k.text: If a split writes the new sibling before updating the parent separator and no latch coordinates readers, a concurrent reader can traverse the old parent and miss keys in the new sibling.

unsafe-scenario-test-demonstrates-stale-.text: `test_unsafe_scenario_stale_write_corrupts` asserts that data corruption occurs without fencing, contrasted with the safe scenario test.

utf8-decode-unguarded.text: If a segment contains a key with invalid UTF-8 bytes, `_scan_segment` raises an unhandled `UnicodeDecodeError` that aborts recovery for all subsequent segments.

values-must-be-bytes.text: B-tree values are written as raw bytes with no encoding; keys accept `str` (auto-encoded to UTF-8) or `bytes`, but values must already be `bytes`

vc-prune-copies-when-within-limit.text: If `max_nodes` is greater than or equal to the clock length, `prune` returns a copied `VectorClock` without performing the sort.

vc-prune-does-not-validate-max-nodes.text: `VectorClock.prune` does not validate `max_nodes`; passing 0 or a negative value returns an empty clock, and passing a non-integer raises `TypeError` from slicing.

vc-prune-is-lossy.text: Pruning permanently discards causal information; subsequent `compare()` or `dominates()` calls treat pruned nodes as counter=0, which can produce false concurrency or false dominance

vc-prune-keeps-highest-counters.text: `VectorClock.prune(n)` retains the `n` entries with the highest counter values and discards the rest, using `sorted` descending by counter

vc-prune-tiebreak-unstable.text: When multiple nodes share the same counter value during `prune`, which survive depends on Python's `sorted` stability over dict iteration order — not a deterministic tiebreak policy callers can rely on

vector-clock-compare-partial-order.text: `VectorClock.compare` returns one of four string values — `BEFORE`, `AFTER`, `EQUAL`, or `CONCURRENT` — implementing a partial order where the symmetric property holds (`BEFORE` ↔ `AFTER`)

vector-clock-immutability.text: `VectorClock` is immutable: `increment`, `merge`, and `prune` all return new instances and never modify `_clock` in place.

metadata.example:
def increment(self, node_id):
    new = dict(self._clock)
    new[node_id] = new.get(node_id, 0) + 1
    return VectorClock(new)  # returns new, never mutates

vector-clock-tests-have-no-error-path-te.text: `test_vector_clock.py` contains no `pytest.raises` blocks and does not test invalid-input or error paths.

verification-impossible-at-every-layer.text: Verification of system correctness is impossible at every layer of the architecture: data integrity verification degrades from partial to absent along the storage pipeline (WAL CRCs exclude metadata, SSTables have no checksums at all), while protocol safety claims are unfalsifiable because all distributed testing uses synchronous simulation that cannot exercise the asynchronous failure modes the protocols are designed to tolerate.

justifications.label: Storage integrity verification degrades monotonically from WAL to SSTable, and protocol safety is tested under the wrong failure model — no layer has a valid verification mechanism

verify-proof-direction-unvalidated.text: The `direction` field in proof siblings is not validated; any value other than `"left"` is silently treated as `"right"` via the else branch.

verify-proof-empty-siblings-checks-singl.text: With an empty `proof.siblings` list, `verify_proof` checks only that `hash(data) == leaf_hash == root_hash`.

verify-proof-hash-consistency.text: `verify_proof` concatenates hex-encoded hash strings and encodes to bytes before hashing, matching the exact same scheme used in `__init__` to build internal nodes — a mismatch would silently break all proof verification.

verify-proof-is-pure-static.text: `verify_proof` is a `@staticmethod` with no side effects; it requires no tree instance, only the data and a `MerkleProof`, so it can run on a different machine than the one that built the tree.

verify-proof-is-stateless.text: Duplicates existing belief `verify-proof-is-pure-static`, which already captures that `verify_proof` is a static method requiring no tree instance.

verify-proof-raises-typeerror-non-bytes.text: If `data` is not `bytes`, `verify_proof` propagates a `TypeError` from `_sha256`/`hashlib.sha256()`.

verify-proof-returns-false-on-leaf-hash-.text: `MerkleTree.verify_proof` returns `False` immediately when `_sha256(data)` does not match `proof.leaf_hash`.

verify-proof-root-trust.text: `verify_proof` confirms data matches a given root hash but does not authenticate the root itself; callers must obtain a trusted root through an independent channel (e.g., a signed block header).

version-scan-includes-unavailable.text: `put()` determines the next version by scanning all replicas including those marked unavailable, which prevents version regression but couples version assignment to unavailable node state.

versioned-kv-store-get-missing-key-retur.text: `VersionedKVStore.get` returns an empty list for a missing key rather than raising an exception.

versioned-kv-store-history-log-is-observ.text: `_HistoryEntry` records every store mutation with action types such as `write`, `sibling_created`, and `reconciled`, but the store's correctness does not depend on this history.

versioned-store-sibling-semantics.text: `VersionedKVStore.get` returns a list of `VersionedValue` entries; concurrent (causally unrelated) writes produce multiple siblings, and the store never auto-resolves conflicts — clients must call `reconcile`

versioned-value-no-tombstone-flag.text: The `VersionedValue` dataclass (`dynamo.py:14-18`) carries only `value`, `version`, and `node_id` with no field to distinguish a live value from a deletion marker, making correct distributed deletes impossible without schema changes

versionstorageinfo-tracks-sstable-levels.text: LevelDB/RocksDB's VersionStorageInfo maintains which SSTables exist at each level and their key ranges, providing the metadata needed for bottommost-level detection.

view-change-contagion.text: Receiving a VIEW_CHANGE from another node causes a non-primary node to broadcast its own VIEW_CHANGE if it hasn't already, propagating the vote through the cluster without requiring all nodes to independently detect the faulty primary.

view-change-requires-2f-plus-1.text: The new primary only acts on a view change after collecting at least 2f+1 VIEW_CHANGE messages, matching the standard PBFT quorum requirement for liveness.

view-never-decreases.text: `_handle_view_change` silently drops any message with `msg.view <= self.current_view`, enforcing monotonically non-decreasing view progression across all nodes.

visibility-assumes-committed-aborted-dis.text: _is_visible assumes a transaction ID appears in at most one of _committed and _aborted; if it appeared in both, the aborted check runs first and aborted would win.

visibility-does-not-check-transaction-ac.text: _is_visible does not verify that the observing transaction is active; callers such as read are responsible for checking transaction activity separately.

visibility-is-pure.text: `_is_visible` is a pure function with no side effects; it reads `_committed`, `_aborted`, `tx.active_at_start`, and version fields but never mutates any state.

visibility-requires-three-conditions.text: A version is visible to a transaction only if its creator committed, was not in the reader's `active_at_start` set, and has a lower `tx_id` — all three must hold

metadata.example:
created_visible = (
    created_by == tx.tx_id or                    # own writes
    (created_by in self._committed and           # committed
     created_by not in tx.active_at_start and    # not in-flight at snapshot
     created_by < tx.tx_id))                     # started before us

visibility-unknown-creator-falls-through.text: If a version's created_by is neither committed, aborted, nor equal to tx.tx_id, _is_visible falls through to the not-in-snapshot case and returns False.

vnode-150-guarantees-sub-1.5-imbalance.text: With 3 equally-weighted nodes and 150 vnodes each, `load_imbalance()` is asserted to stay below 1.5 (`test_consistent_hashing.py:49`).

vnode-count-scales-with-weight.text: Duplicates existing belief `ch-vnode-count-is-weighted` which already captures that a node's actual vnode count is `int(num_vnodes * weight)`.

wal-all-mutations-under-lock.text: Every WAL method that writes records or modifies files (`append`, `append_batch`, `checkpoint`, `truncate`) acquires `self._lock` before performing any I/O

wal-analysis-omits-dirty-page-and-transa.text: WAL recovery only recovers the highest sequence number; it does not build the ARIES analysis-phase dirty page table or transaction table.

wal-append-batch-and-checkpoint-always-f.text: Partially covered by existing `wal-batch-always-fsyncs` and `wal-commit-sync-before-truncate`; also incomplete since `rotation-always-fsyncs` also fsyncs

wal-append-batch-empty-operations-valid.text: An empty `operations` list is technically valid for `append_batch`; it writes a lone COMMIT record and advances the sequence number by 1.

wal-append-batch-invalid-op-raises-keyer.text: If `op_type` is not a key in `OP_BYTES`, `append_batch` raises `KeyError`.

wal-append-batch-lock-held-across-fsync.text: `append_batch` holds `self._lock` across the entire I/O path including the `fsync` call, so other writers block for the full duration of the disk sync.

wal-append-batch-no-try-except.text: `append_batch` has no try/except blocks; I/O errors (OSError/IOError) from write() or fsync() propagate directly to the caller.

wal-append-batch-requires-open-fd.text: `append_batch` assumes `self._fd` is not `None`; calling after `close()` raises `AttributeError` because there is no guard.

wal-append-batch-returns-commit-seq.text: `append_batch` returns the sequence number assigned to the COMMIT record, which is the highest sequence number in the batch.

wal-append-batch-returns-commit-sequence.text: WriteAheadLog.append_batch returns the sequence number assigned to the COMMIT record.

wal-append-batch-seq-num-advances-len-pl.text: `append_batch` advances `self._seq_num` by `len(operations) + 1` (one per operation plus one for the COMMIT record).

wal-append-batch-single-write.text: Duplicates `wal-batch-single-write` which already captures that `append_batch()` serializes all records plus COMMIT into one `write()` call.

wal-append-batch-utf8-encode-error.text: If key or value contains surrogates or non-encodable characters, `append_batch` raises `UnicodeEncodeError` during `str.encode("utf-8")`.

wal-append-increments-seq-before-write.text: In WAL `append()`, `_seq_num` is incremented before the record bytes are written to the current file.

wal-append-mode-no-overwrite.text: `_open_latest` opens WAL files in `"ab"` (append-binary) mode, making it impossible for post-crash writes to overwrite pre-crash records; this is the bridge between recovery and forward progress

wal-append-no-validation.text: `append` performs no validation of `op_type` against `OP_BYTES`; invalid operation names raise `KeyError` from the dictionary lookup, not a descriptive error.

wal-append-not-transactional.text: Individual `append` calls are not wrapped in any transaction boundary; for atomic multi-operation writes, `append_batch` must be used instead.

wal-append-requires-open-fd.text: Calling append after close() raises AttributeError because self._fd is None.

wal-append-respects-sync-mode.text: Covered collectively by existing beliefs `wal-fsync-per-entry`, `batch-mode-defers-fsync`, and `none-mode-never-syncs-on-append`.

wal-append-seq-increment-before-sync-fai.text: If _do_sync() raises an exception after a successful write, the sequence number has already been incremented, so the caller receives an exception but the sequence counter is advanced.

wal-batch-adds-commit-record.text: `append_batch` of N items writes N+1 records to the WAL: the N data records plus a trailing record with `op_type == "COMMIT"` that seals the batch

wal-batch-always-fsyncs.text: `append_batch()` always force-fsyncs regardless of the configured sync mode, because batch atomicity requires the COMMIT marker to be durable before returning.

wal-batch-and-checkpoint-always-fsync.text: The batch aspect duplicates existing belief `wal-batch-always-fsyncs`; checkpoint aspect captured separately.

wal-batch-appends-three-ops-plus-commit.text: Too test-specific; the general principle (batch appends a trailing COMMIT) is captured by `wal-batch-commit-sentinel` below.

wal-batch-atomicity-via-commit-record.text: A batch write is only considered complete if its trailing COMMIT record is present and passes CRC; incomplete batches (missing commit) are discarded during replay

metadata.example:
self._seq_num += 1
data = _encode_record(self._seq_num, OP_COMMIT, b"", b"")
self._fd.write(data)
self._do_sync(force=True)

wal-batch-atomicity-via-single-write.text: Duplicates existing belief `wal-batch-single-write` which already describes the single-bytearray write pattern

wal-batch-bug-is-performance-not-correct.text: The stale `_write_count` after forced syncs causes extra fsyncs (premature batch threshold triggers) but never causes data loss — forced syncs always flush to disk regardless of counter state.

wal-batch-commit-atomicity.text: Duplicates `wal-batch-relies-on-practical-atomicity` and `wal-batch-single-write` — the single-buffer write with forced fsync and its non-guarantee are already captured.

wal-batch-commit-record-has-sequence-num.text: `append_batch` assigns each operation a consecutive sequence number and appends a COMMIT record with its own sequence number.

wal-batch-commit-sentinel.text: Every `append_batch` call writes exactly one COMMIT record (op code 3) as the final record in the batch, with empty key and value fields, consuming one additional sequence number.

wal-batch-counter-reset.text: Misleading given the known bug documented in `batch-write-count-not-reset-on-forced-sync` — the counter does NOT always reflect actual unsynced writes after forced syncs.

wal-batch-mode-counter-resets-on-sync.text: Duplicates existing belief `batch-mode-defers-fsync` which covers the batch sync mechanism.

wal-batch-mode-loses-up-to-n-records.text: In WAL batch sync mode, up to `batch_sync_count - 1` records (default 99) can be lost on `kill -9` because `os.fsync()` is deferred until the batch threshold is reached; only `append_batch()` force-fsyncs regardless of mode.

wal-batch-mode-resets-write-count-after-.text: In batch mode, when `_write_count` reaches `_batch_sync_count`, `_do_sync` performs the fsync and resets `_write_count` to 0.

wal-batch-relies-on-practical-atomicity.text: `append_batch()` buffers all operations plus COMMIT into a single `write()` call to minimize the partial-write window, but the code acknowledges this is not a true atomicity guarantee — a crash during the write can persist a prefix without the COMMIT marker

wal-batch-replay-provides-atomicity.text: WAL batch replay correctly identifies and rejects incomplete batches via the trailing COMMIT sentinel, providing atomic-or-nothing batch recovery semantics.

justifications.label: Batch atomicity holds only when incomplete batches are detectable — without BEGIN markers, replay cannot distinguish standalone writes from orphaned batch members

wal-batch-single-file.text: `append_batch` writes the entire batch buffer in one `_fd.write` call before `_maybe_rotate`, so a batch never spans two WAL files under normal operation

wal-batch-single-write.text: `append_batch()` serializes all data records plus the trailing COMMIT marker into one `bytearray` and issues a single `fd.write()` call, relying on OS write atomicity for small batches

wal-batch-sync-count-controls-durability.text: In batch mode, up to `batch_sync_count - 1` records may be lost on crash because they haven't been fsynced yet.

wal-batch-sync-count-default-100.text: The WAL's batch sync count defaults to 100 writes.

wal-batch-sync-count-defaults-to-100.text: The WAL's `_batch_sync_count` defaults to 100, so in `"batch"` sync mode an `fsync` is issued every 100 writes.

wal-batch-sync-counter-reset.text: Duplicates existing belief `batch-mode-defers-fsync` which covers the batch sync deferral mechanism.

wal-batch-sync-force-override.text: The WAL's `_do_sync` batch mode (fsync every N writes) is overridden by `force=True` in `append_batch` and `checkpoint`, ensuring atomic batch boundaries and checkpoint records are always fsynced regardless of configured sync mode.

wal-binary-format-prevents-evolution-and.text: The WAL binary format is simultaneously inflexible and fragile: contiguous record packing with no block alignment prevents resync after mid-file corruption, signed 32-bit length fields theoretically admit negative values with no guard, and there is no version field — a format change invalidates all existing WAL files with no migration path and no way to distinguish old-format from new-format records.

justifications.label: Format blocks both corruption recovery (no block boundaries) and evolution (no version field)

wal-checkpoint-as-replay-fence.text: Duplicates `checkpoint-record-not-used-in-recovery` and `checkpoint-filtered-from-replay` — the checkpoint mechanism and its limitations are already captured.

wal-checkpoint-bounds-replay.text: Covered by `checkpoint-record-not-used-in-recovery` (caller must supply seq externally) and `replay-strict-greater-than-filter` (replay skips records at or below the supplied seq).

wal-checkpoint-consumes-sequence.text: `checkpoint()` increments the WAL sequence counter by 1, occupying a position in the sequence number space alongside data records (e.g., after 6 data records at seq 1-6, `current_seq_num()` is 7 and `checkpoint()` returns 8).

wal-checkpoint-forces-fsync.text: `checkpoint()` calls `_do_sync(force=True)`, making the checkpoint marker durable on disk regardless of the configured sync mode, so recovery boundaries are never lost even in `"none"` or `"batch"` mode.

wal-checkpoint-forces-sync.text: `checkpoint()` calls `_do_sync(force=True)`, making checkpoint markers always durable on disk regardless of the configured sync mode

wal-checkpoint-is-explicit-record-type.text: Already implied by existing beliefs `checkpoint-record-not-used-in-recovery`, `wal-checkpoint-consumes-sequence`, and `checkpoint-filtered-from-replay`, which collectively establish that OP_CHECKPOINT is a record type in the WAL stream.

wal-checkpoint-returns-seq.text: `WriteAheadLog.checkpoint()` returns the sequence number it wrote, providing the caller the exact truncation boundary for the WAL-to-data-store coordination protocol

wal-checkpoint-seq-is-next-after-data.text: Checkpoint markers consume a sequence number in the same monotonic space as data records — a checkpoint after 7 data records occupies seq=8

wal-checkpoint-sequence-follows-precedin.text: WriteAheadLog.checkpoint() obtains its sequence number after all preceding append() and append_batch() mutations, so a checkpoint returning N guarantees earlier mutations precede it.

wal-checkpoint-writes-op-checkpoint-reco.text: The standalone WAL's checkpoint() method writes an OP_CHECKPOINT record (opcode value 4) with an empty payload into the log stream.

wal-checksum-covers-page-data-only.text: The WAL checksum covers only the page data bytes, not the entry header fields (sequence number, page number, data length).

wal-checksum-is-crc32.text: Already covered by existing beliefs including `btree-wal-uses-trailer-crc` and `all-three-implementations-use-payload-only-crc`

wal-commit-assumes-data-already-applied.text: WAL.commit assumes all page writes logged via log_write have already been applied to the PageManager data file; it only syncs the data file and clears the WAL.

wal-commit-clears-all-entries.text: `WAL.commit` clears the entire WAL unconditionally via truncate; there is no partial commit or transaction grouping within a single WAL file

wal-commit-no-exception-handling.text: WAL.commit does not catch exceptions; failures from page_manager.sync, truncate, flush, or fsync propagate to the caller.

wal-commit-record-has-empty-key-and-valu.text: The OP_COMMIT record written by append_batch is encoded with an empty key and empty value.

wal-commit-required.text: The mechanics are covered by `wal-commit-clears-all-entries` and `wal-commit-sync-before-truncate`; caller responsibility is implied by `btree-insert-no-wal-commit`.

wal-commit-sync-before-truncate.text: `WAL.commit` always fsyncs the data file before truncating the WAL file; reversing this order would create a crash-safety hole where committed data could be lost

wal-commit-syncs-metadata-implicitly.text: `WAL.commit()` in the B-tree engine syncs metadata page 0 because `PageManager.sync()` fsyncs the single shared file descriptor that holds both data pages and metadata; there is no dedicated metadata fsync step

wal-concurrent-write-during-read-can-tri.text: A concurrent `append()` writing to a file the iterator is reading can produce a partial record that `_read_record` interprets as CRC failure, terminating the entire iterator and dropping all remaining valid records across subsequent files

wal-contiguous-no-block-alignment.text: None of the WAL implementations use block-aligned or page-aligned record layouts; all records are packed contiguously with variable-length encoding, so torn writes can land at arbitrary byte offsets

wal-corruption-discards-tail.text: Covered by `wal-corruption-stops-per-file` (stops at first corruption per file, continues to next) and `iterate-stops-silently-at-corruption`

wal-corruption-halts-recovery.text: Duplicates existing `wal-corruption-stops-per-file` (stops at first corrupt record within each file but continues to next file) and `wal-no-resync-after-corruption`.

wal-corruption-returns-valid-prefix.text: When the WAL encounters a corrupted record during replay, it stops and returns all structurally valid records preceding the corruption point rather than raising an exception to the caller.

wal-corruption-stops-all-files.text: Duplicates existing `wal-crc-mismatch-halts-all-replay` which already captures that CRC mismatch terminates the entire replay/iteration

wal-corruption-stops-per-file.text: `_recover_seq_num` stops at the first corrupted record within each file but continues to subsequent WAL files, so cross-file recovery is resilient but intra-file records after corruption are silently lost

wal-corruption-test-overwrites-last-five.text: `test_corruption` injects physical corruption by overwriting the last 5 bytes of the WAL file with `0xFF`.

wal-corruption-truncates-at-boundary.text: Duplicate of already-accepted `wal-crc-mismatch-halts-all-replay`; both describe the same behavior where corrupted records stop replay and only valid prefix records are returned

wal-crash-recovery-test-gap.text: Test coverage observation, not an architectural invariant — someone adding the test would invalidate this belief immediately.

wal-crash-recovery-test-uses-second-inst.text: `test_crash_recovery` simulates a crash by opening a second `WriteAheadLog` instance on the same directory without calling `close()` on the first instance.

wal-crash-safety-via-truncation-detectio.text: Covered by existing beliefs `wal-truncation-vs-corruption-distinction` and `wal-partial-read-is-eof` which already describe the two failure modes and their handling

wal-crc-does-not-cover-seqnum.text: The CRC32 checksum covers only `op_type + key + value`; a corrupted sequence number would not be detected by integrity checking.

wal-crc-includes-op-type.text: The standalone WAL uniquely includes `op_type_byte` in its CRC input alongside key and value, protecting against silent operation-type corruption (e.g., PUT flipped to DELETE) that the other CRC implementations leave undetected

wal-crc-input-excludes-seq-num.text: The CRC32 input is op_type_byte + key + value; seq_num is not checksummed, so a bit-flip in the sequence number is undetectable.

wal-crc-mismatch-halts-all-replay.text: `_read_all_records` catches CRC `ValueError` and stops iteration entirely (returns, not continues), so corruption in any file aborts reading of all subsequent files too.

wal-crc-omits-key-and-value-length-field.text: The WAL CRC32 does not cover `key_len` or `val_len`, so corruption to those length fields is not detected by the checksum.

wal-default-batch-sync-count-100.text: In batch sync mode, `WriteAheadLog` defaults `batch_sync_count` to 100 writes between fsyncs.

wal-default-max-file-size-10mb.text: WAL files rotate when they exceed max_file_size, which defaults to 10 MB.

wal-default-segment-10mb.text: WAL and hash-index Bitcask both default `max_file_size` to 10 MB, while the log-structured Bitcask defaults to 1 MB — reflecting the latter's heavier reliance on compaction with hint files to offset recovery cost.

wal-default-sync-mode-is-sync.text: `WriteAheadLog.__init__` defaults `sync_mode` to `"sync"`, making per-write fsync the safe default that callers must explicitly opt out of for higher throughput

wal-defines-four-operation-types.text: The standalone WAL defines four operation types: OP_PUT (1), OP_DELETE (2), OP_COMMIT (3), and OP_CHECKPOINT (4).

wal-do-sync-branches-mutually-exclusive.text: The `_do_sync` method's `if`/`elif` structure means forced syncs in batch mode skip all counter logic entirely — the counter is neither incremented nor reset, which is the structural root cause of the premature batch-sync bug.

wal-do-sync-false-durability.text: Covered by combination of existing `wal-rotation-creates-unsynced-directory-entry` and `rotation-always-fsyncs`

wal-do-sync-flushes-then-fsyncs.text: `_do_sync` calls `self._fd.flush()` followed by `os.fsync()` to push data from Python's buffer to the OS and then to disk.

wal-do-sync-propagates-oserror.text: `_do_sync` catches no exceptions; an `OSError` from `flush()` or `os.fsync()` propagates to the caller.

wal-do-sync-requires-caller-lock.text: `_do_sync` does not acquire `self._lock`; thread safety depends on every caller holding the lock before invoking it.

wal-docstring-describes-intent-not-behav.text: The `replay()` docstring claims it "skips uncommitted batches" (describing the DDIA concept), but the inline comments and implementation show it returns all PUT/DELETE records regardless of COMMIT presence; the docstring is aspirational, the comments are accurate

wal-does-not-protect-flushed-data.text: Duplicates existing belief `lsm-wal-truncated-after-sstable-write` which already captures that the WAL is truncated after flush, leaving flushed SSTable data unprotected.

wal-durability-effective-on-standards-co.text: The WAL's two-tier durability model provides effective crash protection: critical operations (checkpoints, batch commits, rotations) unconditionally force fsync while per-write sync respects the configured mode, creating a meaningful durability hierarchy where batch boundaries are always durable regardless of the performance/durability tradeoff chosen for individual writes.

justifications.label: Two depth-1 conclusions about WAL durability form a coherent positive model, gated on the macOS fsync limitation — on Darwin, os.fsync() may not flush the disk write cache, undermining the entire durability hierarchy on the development platform

wal-durability-invariant-requires-wal-be.text: WAL correctness requires the WAL record to be durable on disk before the corresponding data file mutation becomes durable.

wal-durability-tiers-lost-during-recover.text: The WAL's carefully calibrated write-time durability tiers (per-write fsync in sync mode vs. batch-only fsync) are completely invisible to recovery: sequence numbers and checkpoints that could distinguish between definitely-durable and potentially-lost records are never consulted, so replay treats all CRC-valid records identically regardless of whether they were fsynced — the write-time investment in durability is wasted.

justifications.label: Write-time durability calibration is invisible to the recovery path that ignores its own infrastructure

wal-encode-callers-pass-utf8.text: All callers of `_encode_record` except for COMMIT/CHECKPOINT pass `key.encode("utf-8")` and `value.encode("utf-8")`; COMMIT and CHECKPOINT pass empty bytes `b""`.

wal-encode-crc-mask-unsigned32.text: `_encode_record` applies `& 0xFFFFFFFF` to the CRC32 result to ensure the checksum is stored as an unsigned 32-bit integer.

wal-encode-header-size-21-bytes.text: The fixed portion of a WAL record (record_length, crc, seq_num, op_type, key_len) occupies exactly 21 bytes.

wal-encode-is-pure.text: `_encode_record` is a pure function that performs no I/O or state mutation; all disk writes (and fsync) are the responsibility of callers (`append`, `append_batch`, `checkpoint`, `truncate`).

wal-encode-op-type-not-validated.text: `_encode_record` does not validate that `op_type_byte` is in the range 1–4; it simply packs the provided value as an unsigned byte.

wal-encode-struct-error-on-overflow.text: `_encode_record` uses `struct.pack` without explicit error handling, so overflow (e.g., seq_num > uint64 max or key length > int32 max) raises `struct.error` to the caller.

wal-encode-struct-format-header.text: The fixed header of a WAL record is packed using the struct format `<IIQBi`, corresponding to record_length (uint32), crc (uint32), seq_num (uint64), op_type (uint8), and key_len (int32) in little-endian order.

wal-encode-total-size-25-plus-key-value.text: The total on-disk size of a WAL record is 25 + len(key) + len(value) bytes.

wal-entry-header-is-12-bytes.text: Each WAL entry begins with a 12-byte header containing sequence number, page number, and data length, each packed as a 4-byte big-endian unsigned integer.

wal-eof-advances-to-next-file.text: An EOF or partial read within a single WAL file causes `_read_all_records` to advance to the next file rather than terminate the entire iterator

wal-exactly-at-limit-rotates.text: A WAL file whose size equals `_max_file_size` triggers rotation in `_open_latest`; only files strictly smaller are reused.

wal-file-size-managed-without-syscall-ov.text: WAL file size management avoids filesystem syscall overhead through tell()-based tracking with soft-limit semantics: the hot path uses fd.tell() instead of os.path.getsize() to avoid stat calls and TOCTOU races, the size limit is a soft cap checked before the next write rather than mid-write, and files at exactly the limit trigger rotation to prevent unbounded growth while allowing single-record overshoot.

justifications.label: Three beliefs establish a consistent file-size management strategy optimized for write throughput that trades exact size enforcement for reduced syscall overhead.

wal-filename-sort-equals-creation-order.text: Duplicates existing belief `wal-segment-naming-zero-padded`, which already establishes that zero-padded filenames ensure lexicographic = numeric ordering.

wal-files-have-no-header.text: Each WAL file is a sequence of back-to-back binary records with no file-level header.

wal-files-sorted-lexicographic.text: `_wal_files()` returns segment files sorted by filename (`{N:06d}.wal`), which equals chronological order since segment numbers increment monotonically

wal-first-new-record-uses-max-plus-one.text: `__init__` sets `self._seq_num` to the recovered maximum, and `append` increments `_seq_num` before writing, so the first new record uses `max_seq + 1`.

wal-flush-fsync-pairing.text: Covered by existing `rotation-always-fsyncs`, `wal-batch-always-fsyncs`, and `wal-commit-sync-before-truncate` which together establish the consistent pairing across all WAL sync points.

wal-flush-truncate-replay-safety.text: If a crash occurs between SSTable flush and WAL truncation, replay re-inserts already-persisted entries into the memtable, which is safe because memtable values shadow SSTable values during reads (last-writer-wins)

wal-force-sync-overrides-mode.text: Covered by existing beliefs `wal-batch-always-fsyncs` (the effect) and `wal-do-sync-branches-mutually-exclusive` (the mechanism).

wal-format-change-breaks-compatibility.text: Changing the CRC input in `_encode_record` invalidates all existing WAL files; a production deployment would require a version byte and dual-path CRC verification during migration

wal-format-has-no-magic-sentinel.text: The WAL format starts with `record_length | crc | seq_num | op_type | key_len` and does not prepend a magic number or sentinel to every record.

wal-four-op-types.text: The WAL defines four operation types — `OP_PUT`, `OP_DELETE`, `OP_COMMIT`, and `OP_CHECKPOINT` — stored as single-byte integers in the binary format.

wal-fsync-per-entry.text: Each `log_write` call forces an `os.fsync`, guaranteeing per-entry durability at the cost of one sync syscall per logged page write.

wal-has-crc32-validation.text: Covered by `wal-crc-includes-op-type` (CRC computation) and `wal-truncation-vs-corruption-distinction` (error behavior on mismatch)

wal-has-no-before-images.text: WALRecord stores only `key` and `value` (the new value) with no `old_value` field, making undo structurally impossible from the log alone

wal-has-threading-lock.text: `WriteAheadLog` in `wal.py:80` uses a `threading.Lock` to serialize `append`, `append_batch`, `checkpoint`, and `truncate`, making it the only concurrency-aware component in the codebase

wal-has-three-sync-modes.text: The standalone WAL supports three sync modes: `sync`, `batch`, and `none`.

wal-has-truncation-raft-does-not.text: The WAL module provides explicit `truncate(up_to_seq)` and file rotation for log lifecycle management; the Raft module has no equivalent despite both being append-only log abstractions

wal-hot-path-avoids-getsize.text: `_maybe_rotate` uses `self._fd.tell()` instead of `os.path.getsize()`, avoiding filesystem stat calls and TOCTOU races on every append

wal-io-errors-propagate-as-oserror.text: The WAL has no explicit handling for disk-full, permission, or I/O errors during `write()` or `fsync()`; these propagate as `OSError` to the caller.

wal-is-redo-only.text: The B-tree WAL uses redo-only recovery (replay logged page images forward); there is no undo log, so incomplete pre-commit writes in the data file are overwritten by WAL replay to restore consistency

wal-is-reliable-source-of-truth.text: The WAL serves as the authoritative source from which the entire storage engine can be rebuilt via replay.

justifications.label: WAL authoritativeness depends on replay correctness; while replay lacks batch atomicity verification, partial batches from crashes can corrupt the rebuilt state

wal-is-source-of-truth.text: The unbundled database's `StorageEngine` is fully derivable from the `WriteAheadLog`; calling `rebuild()` replays the entire WAL and reproduces identical state, making the log the authoritative record

wal-iterate-includes-commit-checkpoint.text: `WriteAheadLog.iterate()` yields all raw WAL records, including `COMMIT` and `CHECKPOINT` records, without filtering.

wal-iterate-preserves-all-ops.text: `iterate()` yields every record including COMMIT and CHECKPOINT markers, providing the raw stream needed for commit-aware recovery logic built on top of `replay()`

wal-iterate-returns-all-record-types.text: The WAL's `iterate()` method returns all record types (PUT, DELETE, COMMIT, CHECKPOINT), while `replay()` filters out COMMIT and CHECKPOINT.

wal-key-value-length-signed-int32.text: Key and value lengths in the WAL binary format are packed as signed 32-bit integers (`struct` format `<i`), limiting each field to ~2 GB and leaving negative lengths unguarded.

wal-lacks-page-lsns-and-active-transacti.text: This WAL implementation lacks before-images, page LSNs, and an active transaction table, so it cannot undo partial transactions or detect whether a replayed operation was already applied.

wal-large-records-no-limit.text: Direct consequence of existing `wal-contiguous-no-block-alignment`; not an independent invariant.

wal-length-corruption-mimics-truncation.text: Covered by `torn-length-prefix-causes-silent-skip` (garbage length consumes valid records, returns None) and `wal-partial-read-is-eof` (short reads treated as EOF)

wal-little-endian-hardcoded.text: The WAL binary record format uses little-endian byte order unconditionally (struct prefix `<`), making log files non-portable across architectures with different endianness.

wal-log-write-callers-are-btree-wrappers.text: `WAL.log_write` is not called directly by external code; it is called by `BTree._wal_write_page` and `BTree._wal_write_meta`.

wal-log-write-errors-propagate-uncaught.text: `WAL.log_write` has no error handling; `struct.pack`, `write`, or `fsync` failures propagate uncaught to the caller, aborting the operation.

wal-log-write-forces-fsync.text: WAL.log_write appends to the WAL file and calls both flush() and os.fsync() to ensure durability.

wal-log-write-single-write-call.text: `WAL.log_write` writes the header, page data, and checksum in a single `write` call.

wal-max-file-size-default-10mb.text: The WAL's `_max_file_size` rotation threshold defaults to 10 MB.

wal-max-file-size-is-soft.text: `max_file_size` is a soft limit; a single batch can push a WAL file arbitrarily past it because `_maybe_rotate` runs only after the write and sync complete
